purpose: A queryable felt-index of AoE2DE gaia artwork so an authoring AI can pick and place art by AESTHETIC INTENT (material, function, vibe, felt), not by guessing from unit names. Given a scene need ('a decayed border with a domestic feel'), an AI filters entries by function/material/vibe_tags, reads felt + use_when, and gets the unit_const to place.

standing_legend.human_felt: AUTHORITATIVE. A human reviewer's in-game walkthrough reaction. The ground truth of taste. Prefer this.
standing_legend.ai_felt_from_render: An AI viewed the actual sprite render (kit dat sprite contact sheet) and reacted. Grounded in seeing, but AI-subjective and lacks in-game context (terrain, scale, player-color, neighbors).
standing_legend.ai_felt_from_metadata: Inferred from name/type WITHOUT seeing the art. Provisional, lowest confidence. Flag for a real look.

field_notes.form: single_artwork | modular_tile_set | statue | tree | plant | prop | terrain_district | marker
field_notes.variant_semantics: single | rotation | variety | variety_pairs | hue_gradient | state_direction | combinatorial | tile_set_topological
field_notes.material: A visual material category: greenery | stonery | woodery | metal | water | ice | bone (+ mixes).
field_notes.function: what the art is FOR: border | maze | enclosure | rug | path | eyecandy | elevation_faker | marker | feature
field_notes.placement_hint: how it wants to be placed: assemble_on_grid (tile-sets) | scatter (eyecandy) | landmark (single feature) | line (borders)
field_notes.sld_size_kb: On-disk .sld size in KB is a rough asset-complexity signal, not a VRAM or crash guarantee. Larger files may bundle multiple scene elements or many variants; small files may contain a single figure.
field_notes.finish: marble | painted. God statues ship in BOTH finishes: marble = antiquity-REMEMBERED (weathered, solemn, museum-white, past-tense); painted = antiquity-LIVED (vivid polychrome, temple-in-heyday, historically true). A per-scene era-feel lever.
field_notes.statue_role: civic-guardian | dynamic-art-piece | wild-shrine | threshold-guardian | triumph-centerpiece | shrine-scene (brings its own setting/offerings) | mixed
field_notes.culture: greek | western-medieval-christian | eastern (buddha/indian) | ... — statues cluster by CULTURAL register; match to the scene setting, not just the role.
field_notes.scale: Each rendered entry may include px_dims (largest-frame content bounds) and a scale_px bucket based on max(width,height): tiny<40, small<100, medium<200, large<320, huge>=320.
field_notes.tree_seasons: DECIDUOUS trees (Oak 349, Birch 1717) pack a full SEASONAL/LIFE cycle into their frame/angle index - not rotations: summer-green, autumn-gold/yellow, bare-winter, dead. Pick the frame for the season/mood. Evergreen + Mediterranean trees (Green Oak, Olive, pines, cypress) stay green across variants. This means one tree unit_const can render a whole season-gradient or a dying forest.
field_notes.tree_index: Forest/canopy: Oak(349 seasonal), Birch(1717 seasonal, pale), Green Oak(2567 evergreen lush). Mediterranean: Olive(1349 gnarled grove), Italian Pine(1348 umbrella), Cypress(2529 columnar spire). Specialty: Asian Pine(2016 bonsai), Wax Palm(2583 tropical), Willow(2025 waterside). Blue Tree(768) + scenario trees A-L pending.
field_notes.scenario_trees: Scenario Trees A-L (284, 400-410) = a mixed decorator tray of SINGLE-LOOK trees (3 facings each, no seasonal frames). Green fill: A,B,C,D,E,H,J,K,L (varied size: D small/bushy, E slender sapling, B tall, J lush, L spreading/acacia). Autumn: G (gold). Dead: F (warm-brown), I (grey). Scatter multiple consts so forests do not look stamped; use F/I for blight, G for fall, L for a lone savanna tree.
field_notes.ground_decals: Fallen-leaves (2029 peach-blossom pink, 2030 maple-red, 2031 maple-gold) are FLAT ground litter decals, not standing plants. Pair them UNDER the matching-season trees to complete a season - gold/red under autumn Oak/Birch/ScenarioG, pink petals under spring-blossom/sakura scenes. Underbrush mats (1352 jungle, 1353 temperate) are ground-cover carpets - a base layer under bushes/trees to kill bare terrain.
field_notes.death_spectrum: The death pieces form a MOOD gradient the felt can select on (death_register field): deliberate-cruelty (impaled 910/2456, vertical & displayed = terror) -> war-dead (skeleton soldier 2518, weapons) -> massacre-innocents (skeleton civilian 2517, farm tools = tragedy) -> anonymous-old (skeleton 710, neutral) -> beast-death/natural-tragedy (animal skeleton 1091, beached whale 2457) -> mourned-tended (graves 820, peace) -> honored-monumental (tomb 2287, reverence+wealth). Pick by the EMOTIONAL BEAT, not just the object: horror vs grief vs neutrality vs reverence.
field_notes.tile_footprint: Each measured entry may include tile_footprint {radius_x, radius_z, tiles, blocks}. blocks:true means units path around it; blocks:false means walk-through decoration. Footprint is derived from game data and does not map exactly to visual size.
field_notes.footprint_calibration: Occupied-tile categories are derived from base radius values: 0=walkable, 0.5=1x1, 1=2x2, and 1.5=3x3.
field_notes.inhabited_world: The inhabited-world set builds a living place across sub-registers: LIGHT (campfire, torches, Asian/paper lanterns, fire shrine), SHELTER (command/army/ornate tents), TRADE (Western/Asian/Mediterranean/Mesopotamian market stalls - 82 variants total; carts ox/mule/asian/broken), DOMESTIC (well, benches wood/stone, barrels, haystack), WEALTH (treasure chest, loot), MILITARY (weapon racks + army tents + command tent = a camp kit), WATER/CIVIC (fountains), FOOD (forage bush, fish trap), GROWTH (scaffolding = being-built, the optimistic counter to ruins). Cultural flavors align: pair Asian lanterns+stalls+carts+pavilion; Mediterranean/antiquity stalls+fountains+classical statues; Mesopotamian stalls+garden+tomb+ornate tent. broken cart + loot bridge into the aftermath register.
field_notes.cultural_statues: s_statue_<culture> (afri/asia/ceas/east/indi/medi/meso/orie/seas/slav) all share ONE placeable unit_const 1279 ("Statue") - the game selects the graphic by culture/region. So placing a Statue yields the LOCAL cultures characteristic monument. Registers: afri=Egyptian, asia=Imperial Chinese (foo-lions+dragon), ceas=Roman (equestrian+columns), east=Medieval knight, indi=Hindu (Nandi+deities), medi=Greek marble, meso=Mesoamerican (chacmool+totems), orie=Near-East (column+ram), seas=SE-Asian Buddhist, slav=Slavic (saints+pagan totem-heads). Distinct from the earlier statue batch (Buddhas/Greek gods/Left-Right catalogs).
field_notes.rock_geology: Rock/geology register: RESOURCE (gold/stone mines, mineable), LANDFORM (3 mountains, all 6x6 - green/snow-capped/jagged - the biggest footprints, build a map AROUND them), DRAMATIC ROCK (beach karst sea-stacks, inland karst pillar-spires, mesa/butte formations), GENERAL (granite rocks1 workhorse, pale limestone), SHORELINE (sea1 small, sea2 cluster). Mountains are landmarks not scatter; sea rocks + karsts pair with water; mesa pairs with desert.
field_notes.ruins: The fall register (paired with death + burned/broken-cart from inhabited). ASSEMBLE-KITS (medi 2234 x20, meso 2350 x18, puru 2514 x12, roman 856 x3 - modular walls/arches/columns/rubble, place on a grid to build a ruined site). MONUMENTAL (castle 1837, church 1838 - single dominating fallen structures). OVERGROWN-CULTURAL (indian 1784 jungle-temple, chinese 1987 pagoda, andean 2611 highland - nature reclaiming). BURNED (greek 2505, achaemenid 2504 - FRESH fire-violence, pair with skeletons/loot; vs weathered stone = old). MYSTERY (old stone head 855 - lost civilization). Weathered stone = old/peaceful; burned = just happened.
field_notes.world_architecture: Intact world-landmark buildings (counterparts to the ruins): SE-ASIAN meru towers (pagoda a/b/c 1201/1202/1203, thatched, tall/med/small); CHINESE pagodas (d/e 2005/2006 tile-eaved) + ceremonial gates (paifang large/small 1990/1989) + columns (huabiao 2058, que tower 2059 - both PAIRED flanking an approach); HINDU shikhara (rekhadeul 1778); NUBIAN pyramids (cushite 1563 intact->ruined); EUROPEAN chapel (1836, intact vs church-ruins 1838). Pair intact+ruined versions for before/after.
field_notes.props_civic: Work + civic + war register (extends inhabited). RESOURCE-INDUSTRY: quarry 914 + lumber 915 (extraction; pair with stone/gold mines + tree stumps as source, crane/scaffolding as use). FOOD-STORAGE: granary 1089 (thatched African) + grain_storage 2501 (mudbrick Near-East silo). CRAFT: furnace 2510 (metal/pottery), leatherworking 2291 (tannery), amphorae 2519 + water_pots 2491 (ceramics), rugs 711 (textile, walkable decal). CONSTRUCTION: crane 2520 (+scaffolding=being-built). CIVIC: sign 819 (wayfinding, implies offscreen places), hero_shrine 2306 (veneration). DARK: gallows 1095 (execution, bridges to death). WAR: gunpowder_keg 2607 + 3 siege sets (2282 equipment=building, 2283 clutter=ground, 2021 props=assembled engines) = full siege-camp kit with army tents + weapon racks.
field_notes.trees_biomes: Second tree wave completes the living-world biomes. CONIFER: pine 350 (seasonal), snow_pine 413, cypress 1347 (columnar; == decorative 2529), monkey_puzzle 2570 (araucaria, prehistoric). TROPICAL: palm 351, jungle 414, rainforest 1146 (69 variants! whole ecosystem), mangrove 1144 (stilt-roots, waterside), brazilwood 2580, lush_bamboo 1984 (+felled 1540). SAVANNA: acacia 1063 (umbrella, scatter SPARSE), baobab 1052 (swollen trunk, landmark), dragon 1051 (dracaena, exotic). SEASONAL-DECIDUOUS (season in frame index): autumn_oak 1248, snow_autumn_oak 1249 (first-frost hinge), asian_maple_green 2027 <-> autumn 2028 (momiji), peach_blossom 2017 (sakura spring, pairs w/ petal decal). WETLAND: reeds 1350 (water-edge). DEAD: dead 1250 (21 variants). Spring<->autumn twins: maple green/autumn, peach-blossom/maple-autumn.
field_notes.final_art: Closes the decorative base. FLORA/FOOD: cactus 709 (desert), forage_fruit 1059 + forage_papaya 2599 (fruit foods) + oysters 2170 (shore shellfish), fernpatch 1175 (rainforest floor). MEADOW CARPETS (large-area, distinct from small greenery tufts): flowerbed 859 (cultivated), flower_1-4 (334-337 wild carpets, rotate for variety), grass_green_patch 301 + grass_dry_patch 1033. WINTER: ice 728 (floe decal). FAUNA (water food, animated): fish dorado 455/marlin 450/perch 53/salmon 456/snapper 458/tuna 457, whale 2625 (largest); land critters howler_monkey 2585 (jungle), panda_rock 2082 (bamboo, id tentative). FLAGS: b 601 (pennant), c 602 (rectangular) round out the a-u family. Flames (FLM*) NOT rendered - legacy .smp format, needs an SMP renderer.
field_notes.coverage: Base decorative Gaia scope: 232 entries, 210 with measured pixel and tile data. Evidence tiers include 6 human_felt and 226 ai_felt_from_render entries. Coverage spans statues, greenery, trees, death and aftermath, inhabited props, work and civic objects, ruins, architecture, geology, fauna, flora, food, and flags. Gameplay units/buildings and legacy flame effects are out of scope. Panda Rock (2082) is an animated habitat vignette with wandering pandas.
field_notes.animation_limit: A contact sheet samples animation as still images and may not show motion or distinguish facings from animation frames. Animated assets may need in-game observation before their motion or variant semantics are treated as confirmed. Known animated vignettes include Panda Rock (2082) and Howler Monkey (2585); fish, whales, flags, carts, and siege engines also animate.
field_notes.client_mods: Client-side mods can change the appearance or scale of base art. Pixel measurements here describe the base graphics rendered by Kit. Modded views may differ; validate exact appearance and variant behavior in the unmodified game when it matters.
field_notes.placement_context: Some objects are culture-selected: a shared unit constant may display the active civilization’s graphic rather than an independently selectable culture variant. Other objects require supporting terrain, such as water beneath fish traps, garden bridges, or water lilies. Distinguish civilization-selected, terrain-dependent, and freely placeable objects; use the game as the final check.

entries.name: Mediterranean Courtyard Walls
entries.material_accent: terracotta roof-tile cap (warm-on-cold contrast is what gives it life)
entries.felt: Not an object, a construction KIT: straights, inner+outer corners, end-caps, and broken/crumbling variants alongside the intact ones. Cold weathered grey-blue stone body with a warm terracotta tile crown. The tile cap reads 'roofed, maintained, human' - without it it's generic rubble. So this is a wall around a LIVED-IN place (villa/courtyard boundary), not a fortification. The decay variants let you build it pristine OR abandoned from one kit - there's pathos in that: a place that WAS kept.
entries.use_when: Enclosing a villa/courtyard with a civilized (non-military) feel; abandoned-estate storytelling via the ruin variants. No junctions, so good for enclosures/corners, not branching mazes.
entries.notable: Includes decay states -> narrative range (kept -> abandoned) from one set.

entries.name: Garden Hedge
entries.material_accent: uniform manicured dark green, no flowers - deliberately plain
entries.felt: Pure topology - a tile-set reduced to graph primitives: straight, four corners, a + cross, an X diagonal cross. Almost a diagram of connectivity. Soft, rounded, uniform dark green, deliberately plain, and the plainness is the point - a hedge should recede as STRUCTURE, not compete as a feature. Felt: order imposed on nature; a boxwood labyrinth, faintly uncanny in its perfect roundedness. Greenery pretending to be masonry.
entries.use_when: THE maze/labyrinth tool - it has junctions (+, X) so it can BRANCH, which enclosures-only sets can't. Also soft formal-garden dividers, hedgerows.
entries.notable: Junctions (+, X) make it a true branching-maze builder; contrast with Courtyard Walls which do corners but not junctions.

entries.name: Mesopotamian Ruins
entries.felt: Ruins as maze walls, graded by material - Mesopotamian is ENTIRELY stone (vs Mediterranean Ruins mostly-stone-bit-green, vs Puru Ruins good-vegetation). Use the material grade to match a scene.
entries.use_when: Stone maze walls / ancient ruined borders where you want no vegetation softening it.

entries.name: Rock Pillar
entries.felt: Natural stone pillars or monumental outcrops create a dramatic vertical landmark.
entries.use_when: A striking natural stone landmark; focal eye-candy, not a border.

entries.name: Tree Dead
entries.felt: The 21 variants are a DECAY GRADIENT, not facings: recently-dead brown at one end -> grey dead-dead at the other. Pick the variant by how long-dead you want it to read.
entries.use_when: Dead/dying woodland; grade the variant to the decay stage you want.

entries.name: AsianMarketStalls
entries.felt: Small family-run shops evoke a lived-in market district; pair with gates and stelae for a coherent East Asian streetscape.
entries.use_when: Building an asian market/town district with a lived-in, populated feel.

entries.name: Sign
entries.felt: 16 variants = two direction-signs in every pointing configuration (combinatorial, not rotation). Choose the variant for the exact directions you want indicated.
entries.use_when: Wayfinding / crossroads markers; pick the variant matching the paths meeting there.

entries.name: Cliffs (Desert / Marble / Terrace / Short / Short Sand)
entries.felt: A 'terrain district' drawn to FAKE ELEVATION - read as wall-terraces or rocky cliffs. Different stone types (desert/marble/terrace/short/short-sand) for the look you want.
entries.use_when: Faking elevation/terracing where the engine's flat; rocky boundaries that imply height.

entries.name: Statue B
entries.material_accent: pale stone body with darker robe patina
entries.felt: A robed figure on a tiered plinth holding a scroll/tablet, mid-oration or reading. Unlike the generic Statue Left/Right sculptures, this one has a ROLE - a scholar/statesman/orator. The scroll reads learning/law/rhetoric; the raised arm reads addressing a crowd. Felt: civic dignity - a forum/town-square centerpiece, a monument to a person of importance, not decorative filler.
entries.use_when: A singular civic landmark at a focal point - forum, plaza, place of importance. Place one, not scattered.

entries.name: GARDENBRIDGE
entries.material_accent: moss + pebble embankment - comes pre-naturalized, reads settled/old
entries.felt: An arched stone footbridge, steps + wooden rails, mossed and pebbled at the base. A SCENE-COMPLETER, not decoration: a bridge implies water beneath and a path across, so it asserts a terrain story rather than just filling space. Comes pre-naturalized so it reads settled/old. Vibe: tranquil ornamental garden - koi-pond, willow, formal-park crossing.
entries.use_when: Over a water channel to make a garden/park crossing; orient the 2 facings to the crossing. Needs water beneath - illusion breaks on dry land. Pairs with the garden district + path work.

entries.name: Statue Athena (Marble)
entries.felt: Warrior-goddess: spear upright, round shield with a gold boss, crested helm, flowing robes on a dark plinth. Austere pale stone. Solemn wisdom-and-war, composed, timeless - the museum/Renaissance idea of antiquity. A temple/civic guardian. 8 facings = rotation (judge the sculpture, not the count).
entries.use_when: Civic/temple landmark, placed singular on its plinth at a focal point; marble finish = antiquity-remembered (solemn, past-tense).

entries.name: Statue Athena (Painted)
entries.felt: Same sculpture as the Marble Athena, POLYCHROME - teal bodice, magenta skirt, gold shield/helm. Antiquity as it ACTUALLY was (Greek statues were painted, not white marble). Vivid, alive, festive - a temple in its worshipped heyday, not its ruin.
entries.use_when: When you want the site to read as LIVING/worshipped rather than ruined; painted finish = antiquity-lived (present-tense, festive).

entries.name: Statue Ares (Painted)
entries.felt: War god as a hoplite - crested helm, spear, round shield, RED tunic/cloak (Ares = bloodshed/war). More aggressive stance than Athena's poised guard. Martial menace; a war-shrine. Polychrome, red-dominant.
entries.use_when: A war-shrine / martial landmark; the red + aggressive stance set a bellicose tone. Pairs with Athena for a war-and-wisdom temple axis.

entries.name: Statue Ares (Marble)
entries.felt: Same hoplite as painted-Ares but austere aged sandstone, monochrome; spear couched (active/attacking) vs Athena's poised guard. A weathered war-hero memorial. Marble = remembered/solemn.
entries.use_when: Martial landmark with a solemn/aged feel; the marble vs painted choice sets ruined-vs-living.

entries.name: Statue Hermes
entries.felt: Giambologna's Flying Mercury - nude, balanced on one toe, arm raised skyward, bronze, in flight. The ONLY dynamic statue in the set: motion, grace, weightlessness. A refined art-piece, not a guardian. Metallic, not stone.
entries.use_when: Where you want elegance/motion/a fine-art centerpiece (a fountain court, a refined plaza) rather than a martial or civic guardian.

entries.name: Statue Artemis
entries.felt: Huntress goddess with a bow and an animal (hound/stag) at her side, base gone mossy/naturalized. A woodland/wilderness shrine - nature-goddess, not civic. The moss + companion read old-forest-shrine.
entries.use_when: A hunt/forest shrine or wilderness landmark, at a woodland edge rather than a city forum.

entries.name: Statue Sphinx
entries.felt: Winged crouching sphinx (lion body, human head, wings), low to the ground. A mythic threshold guardian - enigmatic, watchful, beast-not-god. Sandstone.
entries.use_when: Flanking a gate/entrance IN PAIRS; a mythic/mysterious threshold. Reads as a sentinel, not a monument.

entries.name: Statue Alexander
entries.felt: Equestrian: rider on a rearing horse, sword aloft, cape flowing, on a tall inscribed plinth. The grandest of the set (biggest file). Triumph, conquest, command - the victory-plaza centerpiece.
entries.use_when: THE centerpiece for a great-leader/victory plaza; place singular and dominant. Most dramatic of the statues.

entries.name: Statue Bendis
entries.felt: Cloaked, peaked-cap figure with a spear on a NATURAL round rock base ringed with boulders (not an ashlar plinth). A rustic/frontier/foreign deity (Thracian) - wilder, folk-religion, distinct from the city gods.
entries.use_when: A rustic/frontier/foreign shrine at a wilderness edge; the natural-rock base sets it apart from civic statues.

entries.name: Statue Hephaistion
entries.felt: Robed civilian statesman, one arm raised in an oratory/address gesture, on a square plinth. Unarmed - a civic notable/orator, a forum figure. Kin to the scholar Statue B.
entries.use_when: A civic square/forum honoring a notable; oratory pose reads leadership/rhetoric.

entries.name: Statue Greek Hero
entries.felt: Armored warrior in a muscled cuirass, spear at parade-rest. A composed martial hero/general/champion - dignified, standing guard, not attacking. Sits between Ares (aggressive) and the civilian figures.
entries.use_when: A champion/general memorial; martial but composed. Good default warrior-monument.

entries.name: Statue West (Western monuments set)
entries.felt: A WESTERN/medieval-Christian VARIETY set, not one rotated statue: robed saint/angel figures, a heraldic couchant lion, and celtic crosses. Churchyard, cathedral, castle-heraldry - a completely different cultural register from the Greek gods.
entries.use_when: A medieval/Christian/European scene: crosses for a churchyard/graves, the heraldic lion flanking castle steps (pairs), saints/angels as cathedral or shrine figures. Match to a western setting.

entries.name: Statue A
entries.felt: A single classical robed figure on an ornate dark plinth (1 facing only). Generic classical civic statue, kin to Statue B - a notable/philosopher/deity figure.
entries.use_when: A generic classical civic statue where a specific god isn't needed; single-facing so orient deliberately.

entries.name: Buddha Statue A
entries.felt: Seated grey-stone Buddha with a full offerings tableau at the base (altar, guardian lion, pots, fruit, greenery). A complete devotional shrine-scene in one piece - not a bare figure. Serene, sacred.
entries.use_when: An eastern/Buddhist shrine that should read as actively worshipped; it brings its own offerings/context.

entries.name: Buddha Statue B
entries.felt: THE showpiece - biggest statue in the set. Grand seated green-bronze Great Buddha on a stone platform, flanked by cherry blossoms, a red torii gate, and komainu guardians. An entire Japanese zen-temple scene as one object. Majestic, serene, spring-beauty (mono no aware).
entries.use_when: A major zen/Japanese temple centerpiece; drops a whole temple scene. Place singular and dominant - it IS the location.

entries.name: Buddha Statue C
entries.felt: Gilded GOLDEN seated Buddha (jeweled necklace) on a carved SE-Asian/Thai tiered temple base. Opulent devotion, a rich gilded shrine - warmer than B's austere zen.
entries.use_when: A wealthy/opulent SE-Asian temple; the gold reads riches + active worship.

entries.name: Buddha Statue D
entries.felt: Standing bronze blessing-Buddha (raised hand, abhaya mudra) on a small lotus base. A modest wayside/garden shrine figure - the most restrained of the four.
entries.use_when: A quiet wayside or garden shrine; single devotional figure rather than a grand temple scene.

entries.name: Statue Left (master catalog)
entries.felt: NOT one statue - a 39-SCULPTURE MASTER CATALOG in one unit, addressable by rotation index 0-38. Spans every culture and type: Greek gods & warriors, Chinese dragons & foo-dogs, a golden ox, Buddhas, Western saints & celtic crosses, heraldic lions, tribal totems/tiki-heads, robed monks, classical women. Scale VARIES within it (big monuments to small figures).
entries.use_when: The primary versatile statue source - pick any culture/subject by rotation index. Pair Left+Right for both facings of the same catalog. Check per-index scale before placing (some are monument-scale).

entries.name: Statue Right (master catalog, mirror facing)
entries.felt: The mirror/right-facing partner of Statue Left - the SAME ~39-sculpture master catalog at the opposite facing. Together Left(1343)+Right(1345) give every catalog sculpture in both facings.
entries.use_when: Use with Statue Left to orient a catalog sculpture either way; same index selects the same sculpture.

entries.name: Statue Column (pillar/ruin set)
entries.felt: NOT statues despite the name - a COLUMN/PILLAR set with a full ruin-decay arc: intact Egyptian-capital and plain columns, a weathered wooden totem/tiki carved post, then Greek Ionic/Doric columns with ivy, and the collapse states - toppled drums, snapped shafts, rubble stumps. Felt: the passage of time made placeable. Stand them for a temple colonnade; topple them for a fallen ruin. The ivy + broken drums read melancholy, abandoned-grandeur.
entries.use_when: Colonnades, temple ruins, an overgrown fallen site. Mix intact + broken indices along a line for a decaying-over-distance effect. Scatter the rubble stumps as accents.

entries.name: IndianStatues (Hindu pantheon set)
entries.felt: A devotional Indian/Hindu set, the most ORNATE statues in gaia. Gilded-bronze Nataraja (dancing Shiva) inside a flaming aureole ring - dynamic, mid-dance, multiple facings plus a green-patina aged variant; elephant-headed Ganesha seated (bronze AND pale-stone finishes); a robed standing sage/bodhisattva; and a stone sacred elephant on a plinth. Felt: living faith, not museum-piece - the flame-ring and dance-pose carry motion and reverence the Greek marbles don't. Rich, warm, ceremonial.
entries.use_when: An Indian/Hindu temple, shrine complex, or sacred grove. The Nataraja aureole is a strong focal centerpiece; Ganesha + elephant flank it. Gilded for a wealthy active temple, patina/stone for an old or humble one.

entries.name: Oak
entries.felt: The archetypal big broadleaf. The 42 'angles' are NOT rotations - it's a FULL SEASONAL/LIFE CYCLE in one unit: lush summer green, golden-orange autumn, bare grey winter skeletons, and dead husks. Stout trunk, broad round crown. Felt: the default deciduous forest tree - reach for it when you want 'woods'. Pick the frame for the season/mood you want; mix summer+autumn+bare along one stand for a season-gradient or a dying-forest.
entries.use_when: General deciduous forest, temperate woodland. Choose frame by season: green=high summer, gold=autumn, bare=winter or blight, dead=devastation. Big footprint - it reads as a real tree, not scatter filler.

entries.name: Birch
entries.felt: Tall, slender, pale-barked - the elegant cousin of the oak. Same full seasonal cycle (green summer, yellow autumn, bare pale-white winter skeletons). The white trunk is the signature; a birch stand reads airy and bright where oak reads dense. Felt: northern/boreal woodland, cool light, refinement.
entries.use_when: Northern or temperate woods wanting a lighter, more elegant canopy than oak. The bare white-trunk frames make a haunting winter forest. Season-pickable like the oak.

entries.name: Green Oak
entries.felt: A broad, dense, always-green oak (holm/live-oak feel) - no seasonal bare frames, it stays leafy across all variants. Rounder and lusher than the deciduous oak. Felt: warm, established, evergreen Mediterranean woodland; a park or estate tree; permanence.
entries.use_when: Mediterranean or evergreen forest, parkland, an estate that should look lush year-round. Use instead of Oak when you never want bare/autumn frames.

entries.name: Olive
entries.felt: Gnarled, characterful, low - a twisting trunk under a silvery-green sparse canopy. Reads ancient and cultivated, not wild. Felt: Mediterranean agriculture, old groves, patient labor; each tree looks individual and weathered.
entries.use_when: Olive groves, Mediterranean farmland, an old cultivated hillside. Plant in rows for an orchard or scattered for an ancient grove. Smaller footprint than the forest oaks.

entries.name: Italian Pine
entries.felt: The umbrella/parasol pine: a tall bare trunk lifting a flat, spreading crown - an instantly-readable Mediterranean silhouette. Felt: Roman roadside, coastal Italy, warm classical landscape. Distinctive enough to be a landmark on its own.
entries.use_when: Mediterranean/Roman scenes, avenues and roadsides, a classical villa. Line them for a stately approach; the silhouette does a lot of scene-setting cheaply.

entries.name: Asian Pine
entries.felt: A bonsai-like ornamental pine: curved windswept trunk, foliage in flat cloud-tufted layers. Only 4 variants but each is a deliberate, sculpted pose. Felt: East-Asian garden, zen restraint, cultivated nature-as-art; a chosen specimen, not a forest.
entries.use_when: Japanese/Chinese gardens, a temple courtyard, an ornamental accent by water or stone. Place singly as a focal specimen; don't mass it like a forest tree.

entries.name: Wax Palm
entries.felt: A very tall, slender palm - long bare trunk (some leaning/curved) topped by a feathery frond crown high up. Felt: tropical coast, island, oasis; height and sway. The lean variants give a windblown beach feel.
entries.use_when: Tropical coasts, islands, oases, jungle edges. Cluster a few with varied lean for a natural beach line; the height makes them read even in a busy scene.

entries.name: Willow
entries.felt: A weeping willow: a dense dome of long cascading strands draping to the ground. Soft, graceful, a little melancholy. Only 3 variants. Felt: riverbank, pond edge, a quiet contemplative spot; motion and softness that no other tree here has.
entries.use_when: Waterside - riverbanks, pond and lake edges, a garden stream. A single willow makes a focal, tranquil moment; its drooping mass reads instantly as 'water is near'.

entries.name: Cypress Tree (Decorative)
entries.felt: A tall narrow dark-green column - the Italian cypress spire. Formal, vertical, solemn. Variants differ mostly in height. Felt: villa avenues, cemeteries, a formal garden's punctuation; the strongest vertical accent in the greenery set.
entries.use_when: Formal gardens, villa/temple approaches lined in pairs, cemeteries, a Tuscan hillside. Use as vertical rhythm against horizontal masses; alternate heights for a natural line.

entries.name: Scenario Tree A
entries.felt: A medium green deciduous - the plain default of the scenario-tree tray. Rounded leafy crown, ordinary trunk. Felt: unremarkable-in-a-good-way filler; the tree you scatter to make woods read as woods.
entries.use_when: General forest fill. Mix with the other scenario-tree consts so a stand isn't all-identical.

entries.name: Scenario Tree B
entries.felt: Taller, more upright green deciduous with a clear straight trunk. Reads as a mature specimen among the tray. Felt: a bit of height variation for a forest edge or a yard.
entries.use_when: Forest fill wanting some tall members; mix among shorter scenario trees for a natural canopy height spread.

entries.name: Scenario Tree C
entries.felt: Medium-tall green deciduous, slightly denser crown than A. Another interchangeable tray member. Felt: reliable mid-height woodland fill.
entries.use_when: Forest fill; rotate through A/C/H/K for crowd variety.

entries.name: Scenario Tree D
entries.felt: Small and bushy - almost a large shrub or a young tree, low crown near the ground. Felt: forest understory, a scrubby edge, filling gaps between taller trees.
entries.use_when: Understory and forest edges; sprinkle beneath or between the tall trees to break the 'trees on bare ground' look.

entries.name: Scenario Tree E
entries.felt: Tall and slender with a thin trunk - a young/lanky tree. Felt: a sapling or a crowded-forest tree reaching for light; adds verticality without bulk.
entries.use_when: Dense young woods, regrowth areas; mix with D (small) and B (tall mature) for an age-varied forest.

entries.name: Scenario Tree F
entries.felt: A dead bare tree - leafless warm-brown branching skeleton, some snapped limbs. Felt: desolation, blight, a battlefield or drought; a lone dead tree is a strong mood-setter.
entries.use_when: Wastelands, burned/blighted forest, swamp, an ominous approach. One or two among living trees reads as decay; a stand of them reads as catastrophe. Pair with I (greyer dead) for variety.

entries.name: Scenario Tree G
entries.felt: The autumn tree of the tray - gold/yellow foliage, warm and turning. Felt: fall, harvest season, a mellow melancholy. The only single-look scenario tree with a season baked in.
entries.use_when: Autumn scenes; sprinkle a few gold Gs among green trees for early-fall, or mass them for peak autumn. Use with F/I (bare) for late-autumn-into-winter progression.

entries.name: Scenario Tree H
entries.felt: Medium-tall green deciduous with a slightly heavier trunk base. Another green tray member. Felt: solid mid-forest fill.
entries.use_when: Forest fill; part of the green rotation (A/C/H/J/K).

entries.name: Scenario Tree I
entries.felt: A second dead tree - greyer, thinner, more weathered twigs than F. Felt: older death, long-dead snag, ashen. Pairs with F for a non-repeating dead grove.
entries.use_when: Same as F (wastelands, blight, swamp) but for variety alongside it - alternate F and I so dead stands don't look cloned.

entries.name: Scenario Tree J
entries.felt: Broad, full, leafy green crown - the lushest of the plain green tray. Felt: a healthy well-watered tree, a shade tree. Good as a slightly-featured member of a green stand.
entries.use_when: Forest fill wanting fuller crowns; use as the 'nicer' green tree near a focal point.

entries.name: Scenario Tree K
entries.felt: Medium green deciduous, compact rounded crown. Interchangeable green tray member. Felt: dependable woodland fill.
entries.use_when: Forest fill; green rotation (A/C/H/J/K).

entries.name: Scenario Tree L
entries.felt: The most characterful of the tray - a spreading, flattish-crowned tree with some lean, an acacia/savanna silhouette. Felt: open grassland, a lone shade tree on a plain, warm dry country. Stands out from the round-crowned rest.
entries.use_when: Savanna, open plains, a solitary landmark tree. Use singly for a focal 'lone tree on the hill'; a few dotted across grass read as African/dry-country.

entries.name: Bush A
entries.felt: A small-to-medium rounded green bush, low leafy mound, 6 facings. The plain workhorse bush. Felt: the thing you scatter under and between trees so the forest floor isn't bare dirt.
entries.use_when: Understory, forest floor, filling gaps around tree trunks. Scatter freely; it's the default bush.

entries.name: Bush B (seasonal variety)
entries.felt: A big 54-frame bush set spanning sizes AND seasons - lush green summer bushes through golden/brown autumn ones. Felt: the premium understory bush; enough variety in one unit_const that a whole bushy forest floor never repeats. Pick green for summer woods, brown for autumn/dry.
entries.use_when: The go-to for rich, non-repeating undergrowth. Use the green frames for lush forest, the brown frames for autumn or arid scrub. Best bush for large natural areas.

entries.name: Bush C (flowering/berry)
entries.felt: A flowering/berry shrub - green frames dusted with white blossom, plus golden autumn and fruiting variants. Prettier and more featured than the plain bushes. Felt: a garden hedge-shrub, a blossoming spring thicket, a berry bramble.
entries.use_when: Gardens, spring scenes, a decorative border shrub, or a berry-bramble edge. Use blossom frames for spring, fruit/autumn frames for late season.

entries.name: Bush Green (plant)
entries.felt: A low sprawling green bush clump, more horizontal/S-shaped spread than the round bushes. 8 facings. Felt: scrubby ground cover, the messy real-forest floor.
entries.use_when: Underbrush and scrub; layer with Bush A for varied floor texture. Reads well along paths and clearing edges.

entries.name: Shrub Green (plant)
entries.felt: A small delicate leafy shrub - fern-like sprigs, airier and finer than the bushes. 8 facings. Felt: fine detail on the forest floor, a fern in the shade, a tended garden's low greenery.
entries.use_when: Fine-grained ground detail in shaded understory, garden beds, and grass edges. Roughly one low plant per four tiles is a useful official-map reference within vegetated patches, while worn camp ground stays sparse. Use where a full bush would be too heavy.

entries.name: Plants (small sprigs)
entries.felt: Tiny green sprigs/leaf tufts, barely more than a few blades. 5 facings. Felt: the smallest greenery accent - a weed poking through, a bit of life on bare ground.
entries.use_when: The finest scatter detail between paving, along grass edges, and across vegetated ground. Official-map examples suggest roughly one low plant per four tiles in vegetated patches; leave worn camp ground sparse. Nearly subliminal; use lightly across broad areas.

entries.name: Plant Dead
entries.felt: Small dead twiggy brown tufts - desiccated little bushes/dead brush. 8 facings. Felt: drought, barren ground, winter kill; the dry counterpart to the grass and bush scatter.
entries.use_when: Deserts, wastelands, dead/blighted ground, winter. Scatter with Grass Dry and dead trees for a parched or lifeless scene.

entries.name: Plant (Flower)
entries.felt: Wildflower clumps - green foliage speckled with small white, red, and yellow blossoms. 8 facings. Felt: a meadow, spring, cultivated cheer; the only real spot-color in the ground layer.
entries.use_when: Meadows, cottage gardens, spring scenes, brightening a green field. Scatter for wild meadow, cluster for a flower bed. The pop of color other greenery lacks.

entries.name: Grass Green
entries.felt: Green grass tufts - fresh vertical blades in small clumps. 8 facings. Felt: living meadow, well-watered field, spring/summer ground. The base texture of a healthy landscape.
entries.use_when: Mass across fields and clearings for a lush look, or scatter to break up flat terrain. Pair with Grass Dry at edges for a moisture gradient.

entries.name: Grass Dry
entries.felt: Dry golden/straw grass tufts - the sun-bleached counterpart to Grass Green. 8 facings. Felt: late summer, savanna, drought, harvest stubble; warm and arid.
entries.use_when: Steppe, savanna, dry season, arid edges. Blend with Grass Green for a green-to-dry gradient; mass alone for parched plains.

entries.name: Plant Jungle
entries.felt: Lush tropical floor plants - broad fern-like leaves in green clumps, 8 facings. Felt: humid jungle undergrowth, dense green life. Reads instantly as 'tropics'.
entries.use_when: Jungle and rainforest floors, tropical riverbanks. Scatter thickly under palms and jungle trees for a dense canopy-floor.

entries.name: Plant Rainforest
entries.felt: Taller, more upright rainforest plants - broad leaves with occasional small flowers. Richer and leggier than Plant Jungle. Felt: deep rainforest understory, exotic and layered.
entries.use_when: Rainforest floors wanting height and variety; layer with Plant Jungle (low/broad) for a two-tier tropical understory.

entries.name: Plant Underbrush Jungle
entries.felt: A dense low sprawling MAT of jungle ground-cover - thick leaves speckled with tiny flowers/berries, 9 facings. Felt: the forest floor swallowed by growth; walk-through-it density. Covers ground rather than standing up.
entries.use_when: Carpet a jungle floor - lay these as a base layer, then stand Plant Jungle/Rainforest on top. Great for 'untamed, overgrown' where the ground itself is alive.

entries.name: Plant Underbrush
entries.felt: The temperate version of the underbrush mat - dense low green ground-cover, no flowers, 9 facings. Felt: a thick leafy forest floor, the mat of growth between trees in real woods.
entries.use_when: Carpet temperate forest floors as a base layer under bushes and trees; kills the 'trees on bare terrain' look. Pair with Bush A/B on top.

entries.name: Rock Jungle
entries.felt: Clusters of mossy boulders overgrown with ferns, mushrooms, and jungle plants - a fully decorated rock formation, not bare stone. 6 varied arrangements. Felt: an ancient overgrown outcrop, a mysterious jungle landmark; the rock and the life on it are one piece.
entries.use_when: Jungle/rainforest focal points, a mossy grotto, a ruin being reclaimed by nature. Use as a ready-made detailed feature - no need to hand-decorate the rocks yourself.

entries.name: Fallen Leaves (Maple Autumn)
entries.felt: Flat scatters of golden-yellow fallen maple leaves on the ground - 18 variants from sparse specks to thick drifts. Felt: autumn underfoot, the season made ground. A flat litter decal, not a standing plant.
entries.use_when: Lay UNDER autumn trees (Oak/Birch gold frames, Scenario Tree G) to complete the season - leaves in the canopy AND on the ground. Vary density: sparse at edges, drifts in hollows.

entries.name: Fallen Leaves (Maple Red)
entries.felt: Deep red/crimson fallen maple leaf litter, flat on the ground, 6 density variants. Felt: peak autumn, a richer and moodier ground than the gold. Vivid.
entries.use_when: Under red/late-autumn trees for a saturated fall floor; mix with the gold maple litter for natural color variation. Crimson reads more dramatic than gold.

entries.name: Fallen Leaves (Peach Blossom)
entries.felt: Soft pink fallen blossom PETALS scattered on the ground, 6 density variants. Felt: spring, a cherry/peach orchard in bloom shedding petals, romance and transience. The spring counterpart to autumn leaf litter.
entries.use_when: Under blossoming trees and in East-Asian garden scenes (recall Buddha B's sakura courtyard) for petals-on-the-ground. A drift of pink says 'spring' and 'fleeting beauty' at once.

entries.name: Tree Stump
entries.felt: Small cut tree stumps - the remnant of a felled tree, 9 facings. Felt: logging, a cleared woodland, human hands in the forest; a quiet trace of what was there.
entries.use_when: Logging camps, cleared or clearing forest, a woodcutter's yard. Scatter a few among standing trees to imply harvest; pair with Felled Tree (1539) and cut logs.

entries.name: Bamboo Stump
entries.felt: Small clusters of cut bamboo stalks/shoots - yellow-green segmented stems, 3 facings. Felt: a bamboo grove edge, harvested bamboo, East-Asian countryside. Distinctly bamboo, not generic wood.
entries.use_when: Bamboo groves, East-Asian scenes, a cut/managed bamboo stand. Scatter at the base of taller bamboo or as low accent in an Asian garden.

entries.name: Felled Tree
entries.felt: A toppled tree lying on the ground - a horizontal trunk with leaf litter around it, 6 facings. Felt: deadfall, storm damage, or logging; the tree that came down. Reads as motion-past and decay.
entries.use_when: Logging sites (with Stump 415), storm-struck or old-growth forest, a natural bridge over a small gap, deadwood on a forest floor. One fallen log adds instant naturalism.

entries.name: Water Lily
entries.felt: Floating lily pads on a water surface, some with small pink blooms, 5 facings. Felt: a still pond, calm water, serenity; a flat surface-decal for water rather than land. The one greenery piece meant to sit ON water.
entries.use_when: Ponds, lake shallows, a garden water feature, a slow stream. Scatter across still water to bring it alive; pair with the Willow (2025) and Garden Bridge for a classic water-garden.

entries.name: Forage Pineapple
entries.felt: Clusters of spiky pineapple/bromeliad plants with ripe fruit, 4 facings. Felt: tropical abundance, a food-bearing plant; distinct, recognizable, edible. More 'resource' than pure decoration.
entries.use_when: Tropical/jungle scenes as forageable food or lush ground interest; a plantation or a wild fruiting patch. Its spiky rosette shape stands out against soft jungle foliage.

entries.name: Garden Bridge
entries.felt: An elegant arched stone footbridge with railings, plants and rocks tucked at its feet, 2 facings. Felt: a tended garden, a deliberate crossing, the human-made grace note over water. Complete and ornamental, not utilitarian.
entries.use_when: Over a garden stream or pond narrows, an Asian or formal garden path. Place across water with Water Lily beneath and a Willow nearby for the archetypal water-garden vignette. Pick the facing that matches the water's run.

entries.name: Garden Pavilion
entries.felt: An East-Asian pavilion/gazebo - tiered pagoda roof, red columns, stone platform; variants include single and double-eaved roofs, 3 forms. Felt: a place to rest and contemplate, a garden's architectural heart; refined, cultured, serene. Chinese/Japanese garden centerpiece.
entries.use_when: The focal building of an Asian garden or temple grounds - set on a rise or by water, approached by a path, framed with Asian Pine, Cypress, sakura and the Garden Bridge. A destination, place one.

entries.name: Grapevine
entries.felt: Grapevines on wooden trellis posts - vines climbing a frame, some heavy with purple grapes, across 16 growth/arrangement variants. Felt: a working vineyard, harvest, Mediterranean agriculture and wine. The variants read like growth stages and row pieces.
entries.use_when: Vineyards - line trellis pieces in rows on a hillside; use grape-laden variants for harvest season, barer ones for early growth. Pair with a villa, olive grove, and Italian cypress for Tuscan/Mediterranean farmland.

entries.name: Mesopotamian Garden
entries.felt: Raised brick/stone planter beds filled with cultivated plants - assorted bed lengths and contents, some with ornaments, 10 variants. Felt: a deliberate, wealthy, engineered garden (hanging-gardens energy); nature contained and arranged by hand. Formal, prosperous.
entries.use_when: Palace and temple gardens, a wealthy courtyard, ancient Near-East settings. Assemble beds on a grid to build a formal planted garden; mix contents/lengths for variety. The cultivated counterpart to wild greenery.

entries.name: Sacred Tree
entries.felt: A large lush tree standing on a decorated circular stone base ringed with rocks and plants, 4 variants. Felt: veneration - a tree made holy, tended and enclosed; a village's sacred grove or a shrine's heart. More than a tree: a place of meaning. The base is what elevates it.
entries.use_when: A shrine, a sacred grove, a village center or meeting-tree, a druidic/animist focal point. Place singly as a landmark with reverence around it (offerings, a path, a clearing). The ringed base means it reads as intentional, not wild.

entries.name: Skeleton
entries.felt: Anonymous bleached human bones splayed where they fell - 15 arrangements of disarticulated remains. Felt: old, neutral death; long past, nobody left to mourn. Not horror, just the fact of it. The default 'someone died here.'
entries.use_when: A place death visited long ago - an old battlefield gone quiet, a desert crossing's toll, a dungeon floor, a picked-over site. Scatter singly for a hint, in numbers for a boneyard. Emotionally neutral - use graves/tomb for reverence, impaled/civilian for horror.

entries.name: Skeleton Civilian
entries.felt: Skeletons fallen BESIDE their everyday tools - a bucket, a rake, a pot. Felt: the massacre of innocents. The tools are the gut-punch: these were people doing ordinary work when death came for them. Far more tragic than anonymous bones because it tells you WHO died and that they weren't fighting.
entries.use_when: A sacked village, a slaughtered peasantry, atrocity against non-combatants. Place among ruined houses and broken fences for a raided settlement. Use when you want grief and injustice, not just death.

entries.name: Skeleton Soldier
entries.felt: Skeletons among scattered weapons, shields, and helms - the war-dead. Felt: a battlefield after the crows; men who died fighting. Grim but with a soldier's dignity that the civilian dead lack. The arms beside the bones say how they fell.
entries.use_when: Battlefields, a last stand, a contested pass, the aftermath of a siege. Scatter with broken weapons and (optionally) the impaled corpses for the losing side's fate. The martial counterpart to the civilian massacre.

entries.name: Animal Skeleton
entries.felt: A large animal's ribcage and a skull - a beast's remains. Only 2 variants. Felt: the death of the wild - famine, a predator's kill, a desert that took even the strong. Harsher and lonelier than human death; no rites, no witnesses.
entries.use_when: Deserts, wastelands, a hard wilderness, a drought-struck plain. A ribcage on cracked earth sets 'this land kills' better than any human bone. Pair with Grass Dry and dead plants.

entries.name: Impaled Corpse
entries.felt: A body impaled on a tall stake, still armored - VERTICAL, displayed, meant to be SEEN. 5 variants. Felt: fresh deliberate cruelty; not a death that happened but one inflicted as a message. Terror, tyranny, a warning at the road. The only death here that stands up, and that verticality is the horror.
entries.use_when: A tyrant's approach, a warning at gates or a crossroads, the price of rebellion, a place of terror. Use sparingly - one impaled corpse is a landmark of dread; a row of them is a regime. Strongest horror in the set.

entries.name: Antiquity Impaled Corpse
entries.felt: The impaled corpse in ancient/classical dress - the same displayed atrocity for antiquity settings. Felt: ancient cruelty, a crucifixion-adjacent horror, the brutality beneath a classical facade.
entries.use_when: Ancient/classical scenes needing the same dread as the medieval impaled corpse - a Roman road's warning, a defeated city's fate. Use with Antiquity ruins and the classical statues to keep the era consistent.

entries.name: Graves
entries.felt: Small grave markers - a cross, a headstone, a low mound. 6 variants. Felt: tended, mourned, ORDERLY death. Someone dug these, someone remembers. Peace and grief rather than horror; the civilized answer to dying. Small footprint.
entries.use_when: Churchyards and cemeteries (lay in rows on a grid), a marked grave by a road, a monastery's burial ground. Use when death is honored and quiet, not violent. The emotional opposite of the impaled corpses.

entries.name: Mesopotamian Tomb
entries.felt: Actual stone mausoleum BUILDINGS - tiled-roof tombs, some ornamented. 8 variants, monument-scale. Felt: honored, monumental death; wealth and power outlasting the body. The dead who mattered, housed in stone. Reverence at civic scale, not a scattered bone but a built statement.
entries.use_when: A necropolis, a royal or noble burial, an ancient cemetery of the wealthy, a temple precinct's tombs. Place as landmarks with space around them. The grandest end of the death spectrum - power even over mortality.

entries.name: Beached Whale
entries.felt: A whale carcass, dark and vast, a red wound at its belly. 8 facings, monument-scale. Felt: natural tragedy on a huge scale - a leviathan brought low, mournful and awe-ful at once. Not violence or rites, just the sea giving up its giant. Also a resource (a windfall of meat for a shore people).
entries.use_when: A coastline, a fishing village's grim fortune, a lonely beach. Place at the waterline as a landmark - it reads both as tragedy and as a feast washed ashore. The one death here that is nobody's fault.

entries.name: Campfire
entries.felt: A small log campfire with flames. Felt: warmth, a stopping place, the human instinct to gather around light. The tiny heart of any camp or bivouac.
entries.use_when: Camps, bivouacs, a wilderness rest-stop, outside tents. Place one at the center of a tent cluster; a fire is what turns scattered tents into a CAMP.

entries.name: Torch A
entries.felt: A plain standing torch on a wooden pole. Felt: basic light in the dark, a lit path, a guarded post. Utilitarian, humble.
entries.use_when: Line a path or wall at night, flank a gate or doorway, light a camp perimeter. Pair in rows for a lit approach. The everyday light source.

entries.name: Torch B
entries.felt: An ornate wrought-iron brazier-torch on a tall pole. Felt: ceremonial, grander light - a temple, a palace approach, a place of importance, not a soldier's camp. The dressed-up sibling of Torch A.
entries.use_when: Formal/sacred settings - temple avenues, palace gates, a shrine. Use Torch B where the place has status and Torch A where it's practical.

entries.name: Asian Lanterns
entries.felt: East-Asian lanterns - carved stone pedestal lanterns (Japanese toro), plus tripod and pole types. 10 variants. Felt: serene, tended, contemplative; the quiet light of a temple garden or a shrine path. Refined, not festive.
entries.use_when: Japanese/Chinese gardens, temple and shrine paths, a pond edge or pavilion approach. Line stone lanterns along a garden walk; pair with Asian Pine, Cypress, and the Garden Pavilion.

entries.name: Paper Lantern
entries.felt: Bamboo poles hung with round paper lanterns and strings of glowing orbs. 8 variants. Felt: festival, celebration, a warm-lit street at night; joy and community rather than the stone lanterns' solemnity.
entries.use_when: Festivals, a lively East-Asian street or market at night, a celebration. String them over a market or plaza for warmth and life. The festive counterpart to the stone Asian Lanterns.

entries.name: Fire Shrine
entries.felt: Small stone fire-temple buildings, arched, some ornamented. 8 variants. Felt: fire-worship, a sacred flame kept burning, ancient religion (Zoroastrian energy). A place of devotion built in stone, not a passing camp.
entries.use_when: Persian/ancient Near-East religious sites, a fire-worship shrine, a temple precinct. Place as a devotional landmark; pair with the Mesopotamian tomb/garden/statues for a consistent ancient-East setting.

entries.name: Greek Commander Tent
entries.felt: A grand open-sided pavilion - tiled/thatched roof on posts, furniture (a table, seats) inside, standards at the corners. 3 facings. Felt: command, authority in the field; the general's HQ where the war is planned. The centerpiece of a military camp.
entries.use_when: The heart of an army camp - place it central and larger, ring it with the smaller army tents, a campfire, banners, and weapon racks. Signals 'this is where the commander is.'

entries.name: Greek Army Tent
entries.felt: Peaked canvas field tents ringed with weapons, shields, pots, and gear. 6 variants. Felt: the rank-and-file soldier's camp - lived-in, practical, ready to march. The clutter of arms around them tells the story.
entries.use_when: Military encampments - cluster several around the command tent and a campfire for a believable army bivouac. Vary the 6 for a non-repeating camp. The bulk of any siege or field camp.

entries.name: Tent A (ornate pavilion)
entries.felt: A big ornate round pavilion - patterned fabric dome crowned with a gold finial. Felt: a chieftain's or nomad-lord's tent; exotic, wealthy, mobile power. The Silk-Road/steppe counterpart to the Greek command tent.
entries.use_when: A khan's or sheikh's camp, a nomad encampment, an exotic noble's field seat. Place as the grand tent among plainer ones; pairs with camels, carts, and market stalls for a caravan camp.

entries.name: Army Tent A
entries.felt: A small hexagonal canvas tent with a modest finial. Felt: an officer's or a modest field tent - a step above the rank canvas, below the grand pavilions. Plain, functional shelter. (One of an a-e set of similar tents.)
entries.use_when: Fill out a camp with mid-rank shelters; scatter among the Greek army tents for size/shape variety. Part of a tent_army a-e family - use several for a varied encampment.

entries.name: Flag A
entries.felt: A plain banner waving on a pole (animated across many frames). Felt: a claim, a muster point, someone's ground. Motion in the wind gives a scene life; a flag says 'this place is held.' (One of a large s_flag a-u family + city flags.)
entries.use_when: Mark a camp, a rally point, a held position, a border. Plant at a command tent or gate. For faction color use the many other flags in the family (a-u, plus Athenian/Spartan/Macedonian/etc city flags).

entries.name: Flag Ritual A
entries.felt: A tall standard on a decorated bone/antler-style base - a ritual pole rather than a war banner. Felt: tribal, animist, sacred ground; a marker of belief, not territory. Primal and a little ominous. (One of ritual a/b/c.)
entries.use_when: Tribal or barbarian sites, a sacred clearing, a shaman's ground, an ominous marker at the edge of the wild. Use where the meaning is spiritual/ritual rather than military.

entries.name: Market Stall
entries.felt: Awning-roofed market stalls heaped with goods - fruit/veg baskets, pottery, fish, cloth. A huge 32-variant set. Felt: commerce, a bustling market day, plenty; the single strongest 'people trade and live here' piece. Each stall's wares tell a little story.
entries.use_when: Build a marketplace - line stalls in rows or around a plaza; the 32 variants mean no two need repeat. Pair with carts, barrels, benches, and townsfolk for a living market. The core of any town scene.

entries.name: Asian Market Stalls
entries.felt: East-Asian market stalls - peaked thatch/tile roofs on posts over produce and goods, some with carts. 30 variants. Felt: an Asian street market, a village trade day; the same bustle as the Western market in a distinctly Eastern idiom.
entries.use_when: Chinese/Japanese/SE-Asian town markets and streets. Assemble in rows for a market lane; pair with paper lanterns, Asian carts, and the Garden Pavilion for a coherent Eastern town.

entries.name: Mediterranean Stall
entries.felt: Tiled-roof stalls on stone columns, goods beneath; a couple are bare roofed arcades. 10 variants. Felt: a Roman/Mediterranean forum market - more built and permanent than the canvas stalls, stone and civic. Commerce with columns.
entries.use_when: Roman/Greek/Mediterranean towns and forums, a colonnaded market. Use the bare arcade variants as empty market architecture, the stocked ones as active stalls. Pairs with Italian pine, cypress, classical statues.

entries.name: Mesopotamian Stall
entries.felt: Flat-topped wooden stalls with goods, some open frames. 10 variants. Felt: a Near-East souk, an ancient bazaar; sun-shaded trade in a hot land. The Mesopotamian idiom of the market set.
entries.use_when: Ancient Near-East towns, a desert souk, a caravan market. Assemble with the Mesopotamian garden/tomb, ox/mule carts, and the ornate pavilion tent for a Silk-Road/Babylon feel.

entries.name: Asian Carts
entries.felt: Woven wicker barrel-carts/barrows on a single axle. 6 facings. Felt: humble hauling, a peasant's transport, goods moved by hand. Modest and rustic.
entries.use_when: Asian villages and markets, a farm, a road - parked by a stall or being hauled. Scatter among Asian market stalls for a working-market feel.

entries.name: Ox Cart
entries.felt: An ox-drawn cart (animated unit, 16 facings). Felt: the slow patient movement of goods, farm-to-market, the pace of a pre-modern road. A cart with a beast reads as commerce IN MOTION, not just parked wares.
entries.use_when: Roads, trade routes, a farm or market approach. Place along a road for a sense of traffic and economy; pairs with the market stalls as 'goods arriving.'

entries.name: Mule Cart
entries.felt: A mule pulling a covered cart loaded with barrels/goods (animated unit, 16 facings). Felt: a merchant's caravan, a supply train, a trader on the long road. More cargo-laden and traveled than the ox cart.
entries.use_when: Trade routes, a caravan, a merchant arriving at a town or camp. Line a few along a road for a supply train; pairs with the ornate pavilion tent and Mesopotamian market for a Silk-Road caravan.

entries.name: Broken Cart
entries.felt: Overturned/wrecked carts - a wheel off, goods spilled, timbers splayed. 5 variants. Felt: abandonment, a raid or an accident on the road, hard times. Bridges the inhabited world and the aftermath register - a cart that WAS carrying life, now stopped.
entries.use_when: A raided village or road, refugee trails, a hard/poor place, an ambush site. Pair with skeletons/loot for an attacked caravan, or alone for simple roadside decay.

entries.name: Scaffolding
entries.felt: Wooden construction scaffolding - timber frames, ladders, tools, partial builds, from simple platforms to tall multi-level rigs. 12 variants. Felt: a place BEING BUILT, ambition and labor, a growing town. The rare eyecandy that implies future, not past.
entries.use_when: A building under construction, a growing settlement, a wonder in progress, a quarry/work site. Place against or around a half-built structure; signals momentum and industry. The optimistic counterpart to ruins.

entries.name: Barrels
entries.felt: Clusters of wooden barrels, some tipped, with a spilled sack. 6 variants. Felt: stored goods, provisions, trade cargo; the humble infrastructure of plenty. A few barrels make a spot read as a store, dock, or tavern.
entries.use_when: Docks, markets, cellars, taverns, supply dumps, behind a stall. Scatter to imply stored goods and commerce; pair with carts and stalls.

entries.name: Benches (Wooden)
entries.felt: Simple wooden plank benches. 8 facings. Felt: rest, a place to sit and talk, ordinary daily life; the quiet furniture of a lived-in town. Humble and human.
entries.use_when: Village squares, outside taverns/homes, a market, a garden. Place where people would sit; a bench implies human presence even with no people rendered.

entries.name: Benches (Stone)
entries.felt: Pale stone benches - the permanent, civic cousin of the wooden ones. 8 facings. Felt: a built town, a forum or garden meant to last; more formal and prosperous than wood.
entries.use_when: Roman/Mediterranean plazas, formal gardens, a wealthy town square, around a fountain. Use stone for civic/permanent settings, wood for rustic/humble ones.

entries.name: Haystack
entries.felt: Golden mounds of stacked hay. 3 variants. Felt: farm life, harvest done, animals fed; rustic agricultural plenty. Warm and pastoral.
entries.use_when: Farms, stables, a barnyard, a rural village. Scatter near pastures, fences, and stables; a haystack instantly says 'this is farmland.'

entries.name: Weapon Racks
entries.felt: A-frame racks of spears and polearms, some with a shield and helm set down. 8 variants. Felt: readiness, a muster, an armory; men-at-arms nearby even if unseen. Martial order.
entries.use_when: Military camps (with the army tents), a barracks yard, an armory, a guard post. Place near the command tent and campfire to build a believable army camp.

entries.name: Treasure Chest
entries.felt: A wooden chest - closed, and open overflowing with gold. 4 variants. Felt: reward, a prize, hidden wealth; the promise or payoff of a quest. Small but high-charge - a chest draws the eye and says 'this matters.'
entries.use_when: A quest reward, a hidden hoard, a vault, a dragon's lair, a market's till. Place the open/gold variant as a discovered prize, the closed one as a locked mystery. A focal incentive object.

entries.name: Loot
entries.felt: Big scattered piles of plunder - coins, pots, arms, goods, one with a body, one a bright gold heap. 9 variants. Felt: spoils, a sacked hoard, the aftermath of victory (or greed); abundance with an undertone of how it was got. Bridges wealth and aftermath.
entries.use_when: A dragon's/bandit's hoard, a sacked treasury, spoils after a battle, a pirate cache. Use the body-strewn variants for grim plunder, the clean gold pile for a fantasy hoard. Larger and messier than the tidy treasure chest.

entries.name: Well
entries.felt: Stone wells with a bucket crank, one roofed with a canopy. 4 variants. Felt: THE center of village daily life - where people draw water and meet. Homely, essential, communal. A well says 'people live here and have for a while.'
entries.use_when: Village and town centers, a courtyard, a farmstead. Place centrally as a gathering point; ring with benches and homes. One of the strongest 'settled community' signals.

entries.name: Fountain
entries.felt: Ornate fountains - a figure statue on a tiered basin of water, decorated stone. 3 variants. Felt: civic pride, prosperity, a town that can spend on beauty; the refined heart of a plaza. Water as decoration, not necessity.
entries.use_when: Town squares, wealthy courtyards, a palace garden, a plaza centerpiece. Ring with stone benches and paving; signals a prosperous, established, cultured settlement.

entries.name: Fountain Antiquity
entries.felt: Classical fountains - some figure-topped, some plain lily-dotted basins. 8 variants. Felt: ancient civic refinement, a Roman/Greek forum, engineered beauty and water. The antiquity idiom of the fountain.
entries.use_when: Roman/Greek forums and villas, an ancient plaza or bath complex. Pair with Mediterranean stalls, classical statues, Italian pine and cypress for a coherent antiquity town center.

entries.name: Forage Bush
entries.felt: The classic green bush laden with red berries. 4 variants. Felt: food from the wild, foraging, the earliest sustenance; homely abundance. Instantly recognizable as the AoE berry bush.
entries.use_when: Near a town center or camp as gatherable food, a wild forageable patch, a hedgerow with fruit. Cluster for a berry patch; reads as both decoration and resource.

entries.name: Fish Trap
entries.felt: A woven basket/weir fish trap (animated). Felt: coastal subsistence, patient fishing, a shore people's food; humble water-industry. The maritime counterpart to the forage bush.
entries.use_when: Shorelines, fishing villages, a dock or river. Place in shallows near a village; pairs with reeds, boats, and shore rocks for a fishing settlement.

entries.name: Statue (African)
entries.felt: African/Egyptian statuary: a seated pharaonic ruler on a hieroglyph-inscribed plinth, plus a small carved ancestor/fertility idol. Felt: deep antiquity, divine kingship, the weight of the Nile and older Africa. Solemn, monumental.
entries.use_when: Egyptian temples and Nile settings, an African kingdom, an ancient ruler's monument. The grand seated figure as a temple centerpiece; the small idol as a shrine or village fetish.

entries.name: Statue (Asian/Chinese)
entries.felt: Imperial Chinese statuary (13 variants): robed sages/warriors, guardian foo-lions in stone and gilded bronze, and a coiled dragon on a plinth. Felt: dynastic authority, protection, order; the guardians at a gate and the dragon of the throne. The richest of the culture sets.
entries.use_when: Chinese palaces, temples, and gate approaches - flank an entrance with paired foo-lions, set the dragon as an imperial centerpiece. Pairs with the Garden Pavilion, paifang gates, pagodas, Asian lanterns.

entries.name: Statue (Roman/Caesar)
entries.felt: Roman statuary: a bronze equestrian statue (an emperor/general on horseback on a rocky base), inscribed classical columns, and a small idol. Felt: imperial triumph, civic power, the state made monument. The equestrian is a strong triumphal centerpiece.
entries.use_when: Roman forums, a triumphal avenue, an imperial city. The equestrian bronze as a plaza's heart; the columns as civic punctuation. Pairs with Mediterranean stalls/fountains, the amphitheatre, and antiquity ruins.

entries.name: Statue (Eastern/Medieval)
entries.felt: Medieval European statuary (8 variants): armored knight/soldier figures on plinths - shields, swords, cloaks. Felt: martial honor, a fallen hero remembered, chivalric memory. Formal and dignified; a monument to war-service.
entries.use_when: Medieval castles, town squares, a war memorial, a knight's tomb or hall. Place a knight statue at a keep gate or plaza; pairs with the medieval walls and rubble/ruins for a European setting.

entries.name: Statue (Indian)
entries.felt: Hindu statuary (6 variants): gilded seated deities (a musician/Krishna-like figure) and a golden reclining Nandi bull. Felt: devotion, divine play and sacred animals, warm gilded reverence. Kin to the ornate IndianStatues set but as civic monuments.
entries.use_when: Hindu temples and shrines, an Indian palace or sacred precinct. The Nandi bull before a Shiva temple; the deities as shrine centerpieces. Pairs with the IndianStatues set and rekhadeul temple.

entries.name: Statue (Mediterranean/Greek)
entries.felt: Classical Greek marble statuary (10 variants): robed philosophers, a helmeted Athena-type, draped women and gods in white stone. Felt: reason, ideal beauty, the classical canon; cool, elegant, humanist. The Greco-Roman high-culture register.
entries.use_when: Greek/Roman temples, an academy or forum, a cultured villa. Line an approach with philosophers, set Athena at a temple. Pairs with the Athena/Ares/Hermes statues already felt, marble finish, Italian pine and cypress.

entries.name: Statue (Mesoamerican)
entries.felt: Mesoamerican statuary (11 variants): blocky carved totem-pillars and stone idols, and a reclining chacmool figure. Felt: primal power, blood-and-sun religion, a heavy stone weight; awe with an ominous edge. Angular and monumental, unlike the flowing classical figures.
entries.use_when: Aztec/Maya temples and plazas, a jungle pyramid, a sacrificial precinct. The chacmool at a temple summit; totem-idols lining a sacred way. Pairs with jungle greenery, the cushite pyramid, and stone-head pieces.

entries.name: Statue (Oriental/Near-East)
entries.felt: Near-Eastern statuary (only 3): an inscribed column and bronze animal statues (a ram/goat on a plinth). Felt: ancient Levant/Persia, sacred animals and civic columns; spare and old. The smallest culture set.
entries.use_when: Persian/Levantine/Mesopotamian settings, a temple or palace with sacred-animal iconography. Pairs with the Mesopotamian garden/tomb/stalls, fire shrine, and ornate pavilion tent for an ancient-East scene.

entries.name: Statue (Southeast Asian)
entries.felt: Southeast-Asian Buddhist statuary (8 variants): gilded seated Buddhas, guardian lions, and standing deities on tiered temple plinths. Felt: serene devotion, Khmer/Thai temple splendor, gold against stone. Ornate, reverent, warm.
entries.use_when: Khmer/Thai/Burmese temples, a jungle wat, a Buddhist shrine complex. Seated Buddha as centerpiece on its tiered base, guardian lions flanking stairs. Pairs with jungle greenery, lush bamboo, and the Buddhas already felt.

entries.name: Statue (Slavic)
entries.felt: Slavic statuary (7 variants): robed scholar/saint figures on plinths AND weathered pagan totem-head posts (bearded stone idols). Felt: a culture between two faiths - Orthodox sanctity and older pagan idol-worship side by side. The stone-head totems are primal and a little eerie; the saints, solemn.
entries.use_when: Eastern-European/Rus settings, a village between Christian and pagan, a sacred grove or churchyard. Use the totem-heads for pagan/old-belief sites, the saint figures for Orthodox ones - or mix for a culture in transition.

entries.name: Gold Mine
entries.felt: Clusters of glittering gold ore/nuggets. 7 variants. Felt: buried wealth, the promise of riches, a strike; the raw form of the gold that fills treasure chests. Both a gameplay resource and a geological accent.
entries.use_when: A mining site, a gold-rich hillside, a resource node. Cluster for a rich vein; pair with quarry/lumber camps and mountains for a mining region. Reads as mineable resource.

entries.name: Stone Mine
entries.felt: Pale grey-white stone ore piles. 7 variants. Felt: raw building material, the bones of walls and towers before they're cut; humble industry. The stone counterpart to the gold mine.
entries.use_when: Quarries, a stone-rich outcrop, a resource node near a build site. Pair with the quarry prop and scaffolding for a construction economy. Mineable resource.

entries.name: Mountain (Green)
entries.felt: A big grass-cloaked mountain - conical, green lower slopes, bare rock crown. Blocks 6x6, the largest footprint in the compendium. Felt: permanence, scale, the horizon itself; a temperate peak that anchors a whole landscape. Not scenery you scatter - a landmark you build a map around.
entries.use_when: A map's backdrop or centerpiece massif, a mountain pass, a highland border. Place as a singular landform; its 6x6 block genuinely shapes pathing. Temperate/lush setting.

entries.name: Mountain (Snow-capped)
entries.felt: A snow-capped mountain - white peak over dark rock, thin grass at the foot. 6x6. Felt: alpine majesty, cold height, a hard climb; the roof of a cold land. Grander and colder than the green mountain.
entries.use_when: Alpine/northern maps, a snowy pass, a highland kingdom's backdrop. Pair with snow trees (snow pine/autumn oak) and ice decals for a cold-climate massif.

entries.name: Mountain (Jagged Snow)
entries.felt: A sharper, more jagged snow-streaked peak - pointed and severe. 6x6. Felt: a formidable, dramatic summit; the unforgiving high country. The most dramatic of the three mountains.
entries.use_when: A dramatic mountain skyline, an impassable range, a legendary peak. Mix with the other two mountains for a varied range rather than repeating one silhouette.

entries.name: Beach Rock (Karst Stacks)
entries.felt: Tall eroded karst sea-stacks crowned with vegetation - some arched, some towering pillars (Ha Long Bay energy). 8 variants. Felt: dramatic exotic coastline, ancient erosion, a scene-stealing seascape. Vertical and striking.
entries.use_when: Exotic coasts and bays, an island channel, a scenic waterway. Place rising from water as landmarks; the arched variants frame a passage. Pairs with tropical/jungle greenery.

entries.name: Rock Formation (Mesa)
entries.felt: Layered flat-topped sandstone stacks - warm-toned stratified rock (desert butte/mesa/hoodoo). 4 variants. Felt: an arid canyon country, wind-carved time, the American-Southwest/badlands look. Sculptural and warm.
entries.use_when: Deserts, canyons, badlands, an arid plateau. Cluster buttes for a mesa landscape; pair with cactus, dry grass, and sand cliffs. Warm-climate geology.

entries.name: Rock (Limestone)
entries.felt: Pale limestone boulder clusters with a little greenery. 4 variants. Felt: bright, clean rock; a Mediterranean or temperate hillside outcrop. Lighter and gentler than the grey granite rocks.
entries.use_when: Mediterranean hillsides, a pale-stone outcrop, dressing a slope or path edge. Scatter for natural rockiness; pairs with olive/cypress and Mediterranean settings.

entries.name: Rock Pillar (Karst Spire)
entries.felt: Tall stratified rock spires topped with trees - inland karst columns (Zhangjiajie/Avatar-mountains energy). 4 variants. Felt: mystical vertical wilderness, a hidden highland, otherworldly scale. Dramatic and exotic.
entries.use_when: Exotic Asian highlands, a mystical wilderness, a dramatic inland backdrop. Cluster spires for a karst forest; pairs with Asian pine, lush bamboo, and jungle.

entries.name: Rocks (Granite)
entries.felt: Grey granite boulder clusters, mid-sized. 6 variants. Felt: plain natural rockiness, the default 'there are rocks here'; grounded and unremarkable in a useful way. The workhorse rock scatter.
entries.use_when: Any natural terrain wanting rockiness - hillsides, riverbanks, a rough field, a mountain foot. The general-purpose rock; scatter freely to break up bare ground.

entries.name: Sea Rock (Small)
entries.felt: A small low cluster of dark wet rocks. Felt: the waterline, rocks just breaking the surface, a hazard to a hull. Humble shoreline detail.
entries.use_when: Shorelines and shallows, a rocky beach, a reef hazard. Scatter at the water's edge; pairs with sea2, beach karsts, and reeds for a rocky coast.

entries.name: Sea Rock (Cluster)
entries.felt: Clusters of dark water-worn rocks, some with pale tops. 6 variants. Felt: a rocky shore or reef, waves breaking, treacherous water. More substantial than sea1.
entries.use_when: Rocky coasts, reefs, a dangerous approach, tide pools. Line a shoreline or scatter as reef hazards; the larger sibling of the small sea rock.

entries.name: Roman Ruins
entries.felt: Scattered white-marble ruin fragments - toppled column drums, broken pedestals, a standing column stub. 3 arrangements. Felt: fallen Rome, glory undone, the classical world in pieces. Elegiac.
entries.use_when: A ruined forum or temple, an overgrown classical site. Assemble fragments with the larger Mediterranean-ruins kit for a fuller fallen city; pairs with the amphitheatre/aqueduct rubble and the death batch.

entries.name: Mediterranean Ruins
entries.felt: A comprehensive 20-piece Mediterranean ruin KIT - broken walls, arches, standing and fallen column pairs, doorways, rubble in pale stone. Felt: a whole ruined settlement in modular parts; the richest tool for building a believable classical/Mediterranean ruin. More construction-set than single object.
entries.use_when: Build a ruined town/temple site piece by piece on a grid - walls for footprint, arches and columns for verticality, rubble to fill. THE go-to ruins kit for Mediterranean settings.

entries.name: Mesopotamian Ruins
entries.felt: An 18-piece Near-East ruin kit in warm tan mudbrick - broken brick walls, doorway arches, column stubs, rubble. Felt: an ancient fallen city of the Fertile Crescent, sun-baked and crumbling; older and earthier than the stone Mediterranean ruins.
entries.use_when: Ruined Mesopotamian/Babylonian/Persian sites. Assemble on a grid; pair with the Mesopotamian garden/tomb/stalls and burned Achaemenid buildings for a sacked ancient-East city.

entries.name: Indian Ruins
entries.felt: Ornately carved stone ruins reclaimed by jungle - a vine-covered carved arch, a temple gateway with a palm growing from its roof. 4 variants. Felt: a lost temple swallowed by the forest, Angkor-energy; beauty and decay entwined, mysterious and romantic.
entries.use_when: A jungle-lost Hindu/SE-Asian temple, an overgrown sacred site, an explorer's discovery. Place among jungle greenery and karst pillars; the palm-topped gate is a strong focal landmark.

entries.name: Chinese Ruins
entries.felt: Ruined East-Asian buildings - a broken tiled-roof pagoda/hall, stone gateways with bamboo pushing through. 4 variants. Felt: an abandoned Chinese temple or estate, dynasty passed, nature returning. Quiet melancholy in an Eastern key.
entries.use_when: Abandoned Chinese/Asian temples and estates, an overgrown mountain shrine. Pair with lush bamboo, Asian pine, and karst pillars; the ruined counterpart to the intact pagodas.

entries.name: Andean Ruins
entries.felt: Mossy highland stone ruins with thatched huts - a round thatch hut on a stone base, ruined walls under moss. 4 variants. Felt: a highland Andean/Inca settlement abandoned to the mountains, humble and remote; the cold-country cousin of the jungle ruins.
entries.use_when: Andean/highland ruins, a mountain village lost to time, an Inca site. Pair with mountains, dry grass, and llamas-adjacent settings; humbler and smaller than the grand stone ruins.

entries.name: Puru Ruins
entries.felt: A 12-piece terracotta-toned ruin kit (Puru/ancient-Indian) - broken brick walls, column-arches, fallen columns, a small canopy shrine. Felt: a warm-stone Indian city fallen, assembleable into a ruined complex; the Indian-subcontinent counterpart to the Mediterranean/Mesopotamian kits.
entries.use_when: Ruined ancient-Indian sites. Assemble on a grid for a fallen city; pair with the IndianStatues, rekhadeul temple, and jungle greenery. Warmer-toned than the other ruin kits.

entries.name: Castle Ruins
entries.felt: Massive crumbling castle keeps on rocky bases - collapsed towers, broken curtain walls, a fortress gutted. 2 variants, monumental scale. Felt: a fallen stronghold, a dynasty's power broken, grand tragedy; the most imposing ruin in the set. A landmark that dominates.
