entries.use_when: A ruined castle as a map centerpiece, a haunted fortress, a contested strongpoint's aftermath. Place singly on high or rocky ground; it commands the scene. Pairs with medieval walls-rubble and the death batch.

entries.name: Church Ruins
entries.felt: A large ruined church/manor - collapsed tiled roofs, broken stone walls, a gothic building fallen in on itself. Monument-scale. Felt: faith or nobility undone, a sacred/grand place desecrated; solemn and heavy. Kin to the castle ruin but sacred rather than martial.
entries.use_when: A ruined monastery/church, a sacked town's centerpiece, a haunted holy site. Pair with graves and the death batch for a desecrated churchyard; a strong European ruin landmark.

entries.name: Burned Building (Greek)
entries.felt: Burned buildings - charred timbers, collapsed and blackened roofs, stone walls scorched. 6 variants. Felt: RECENT violence, a town put to the torch, still-smoking aftermath. Fresher and more violent than the weathered stone ruins - this just happened.
entries.use_when: A sacked/raided village, war's immediate aftermath, a razed settlement. Scatter with skeletons, broken carts, and loot for a fresh atrocity; use where the stone ruins would read as too old/peaceful.

entries.name: Burned Building (Achaemenid)
entries.felt: Burned Persian/Achaemenid buildings - charred, collapsed stone structures. 6 variants. Felt: the same fresh fire-violence in an ancient-East idiom; a sacked Persian town. Pairs with the Mesopotamian ruins for a burned-then-weathered progression.
entries.use_when: A sacked ancient-East city (with Mesopotamian ruins/garden/tomb), the aftermath of conquest. Use the burned buildings for the fresh destruction, the mudbrick ruins for what remains after years.

entries.name: Old Stone Head
entries.felt: Mossy carved colossal stone heads lying half-buried and overgrown (Olmec-style). 3 variants. Felt: a lost civilization, deep mystery, a face staring up from the jungle floor after millennia. Eerie, evocative, a discovery.
entries.use_when: A lost-civilization site, a jungle mystery, an ancient overgrown monument. Place singly as an enigmatic landmark among jungle greenery; strong 'what happened here?' charge.

entries.name: Pagoda A (Meru Tower, tall)
entries.felt: A tall multi-tiered thatched meru tower - 6 shrinking hip-roofs stacked to a gold finial over a dark carved base. Felt: soaring devotion, a temple reaching skyward; Balinese/Nepalese sacred architecture. Striking vertical landmark.
entries.use_when: SE-Asian/Hindu-Buddhist temple complexes, a shrine centerpiece, a temple courtyard (recall Buddha B's temple scene). Place as a vertical focal point; pairs with jungle, seas/indi statues.

entries.name: Pagoda B (Meru Tower, medium)
entries.felt: A 3-tiered thatched meru shrine - the shorter sibling of Pagoda A, same idiom. Felt: a lesser temple or side-shrine; devotion at human scale. Complements the tall tower without competing.
entries.use_when: Secondary shrines in a temple complex, a village temple. Mix with Pagoda A (tall) and C (small) for a varied SE-Asian sacred compound.

entries.name: Pagoda C (Shrine Pavilion)
entries.felt: A single hip-roof thatched pavilion/shrine with hanging decorations. Felt: a small offering-shrine, a wayside altar; intimate devotion. The smallest of the meru set.
entries.use_when: Wayside shrines, a temple courtyard's minor altars, a village sacred spot. Scatter among the larger meru towers or place alone at a path or gate.

entries.name: Pagoda D (Chinese)
entries.felt: A classic ornate Chinese pagoda - stacked grey-tile eaves, red columns, hexagonal, railed base. 2 facings. Felt: imperial refinement, a garden or temple's crown; the picture-book Chinese pagoda. Elegant and dignified.
entries.use_when: Chinese temples, gardens, and estates - a lake pavilion, a temple centerpiece. Pairs with the Garden Pavilion, paifang gates, Asian statues/lanterns; the intact counterpart to the Chinese ruins.

entries.name: Pagoda E (Chinese Tower)
entries.felt: A tall Chinese pagoda tower - 5+ tiers of grey-tile eaves on a hexagonal stone base with steps. 2 facings. Felt: a temple's great tower, a city landmark visible for miles; height and permanence. Grander than Pagoda D.
entries.use_when: A major Chinese temple or city landmark, a hilltop tower. Place as the tallest built feature; pairs with the karst pillars and mountains for a classic Chinese-landscape skyline.

entries.name: Paifang Gate (Large)
entries.felt: A grand three-bay Chinese ceremonial archway - red columns, stacked tiled roofs, calligraphy panels. 2 facings. Felt: a threshold of importance, the entrance to a district or temple, civic pride; you PASS THROUGH into somewhere that matters.
entries.use_when: The entrance to a Chinese city, temple precinct, or grand avenue. Straddle a road or path as a ceremonial threshold; pairs with pagodas, huabiao columns, market stalls.

entries.name: Paifang Gate (Small)
entries.felt: A single-bay Chinese ceremonial gate - the modest paifang. Felt: a smaller threshold, a garden or lane entrance; ceremony at a humbler scale. Same meaning as the large gate, lighter footprint.
entries.use_when: A garden entrance, a lane, a minor precinct threshold. Use where the grand three-bay gate would be too much; pairs identically with Chinese architecture.

entries.name: Huabiao Totem
entries.felt: An ornamental carved white-stone column - dragon-and-cloud relief winding up to a crowning beast (a huabiao). 2 facings. Felt: imperial ceremony, the pillars before a palace gate; dignified and auspicious. Meant to be PAIRED, flanking an approach.
entries.use_when: Before a Chinese palace, tomb, or ceremonial gate - place a matched pair flanking the approach. Pairs with paifang gates and the imperial Chinese statues.

entries.name: Que Tower
entries.felt: Carved stone ceremonial gate-towers with tiled caps (Han-dynasty que). 4 variants. Felt: ancient imperial authority, the stone sentinels at a tomb or palace road; older and heavier than the wooden gates. Also meant to be paired.
entries.use_when: An ancient Chinese tomb approach, a palace or spirit road, flanking a ceremonial way (as a pair). More archaic than the paifang; pairs with the Chinese statues and Mesopotamian/ancient settings.

entries.name: Rekhadeul Temple
entries.felt: A tall carved terracotta Hindu shikhara temple - the beehive/curvilinear spire (Odisha rekha deul) densely carved top to base, crowned with an amalaka. Felt: intense devotion made stone, upward-striving sacred geometry; ornate, warm, awe-inspiring. One of the most beautiful buildings in the set.
entries.use_when: A Hindu temple complex, an Indian sacred city, a river-ghat temple. Place as the devotional centerpiece; pairs with the IndianStatues, indi cultural statue, Puru ruins, and jungle greenery.

entries.name: Cushite Pyramid
entries.felt: Steep-sided Nubian/Kushite pyramids with entrance chapels - intact through partially-collapsed. 6 variants. Felt: an African desert kingdom's monumental dead, Meroe's royal tombs; steeper and narrower than Egyptian pyramids, distinctly Kushite. Ancient and imposing.
entries.use_when: Nubian/Kushite/African desert settings, a royal necropolis, a desert kingdom. Cluster the variants (intact + ruined) for a pyramid field like Meroe; pairs with the African statue, desert sand, and mesa rocks.

entries.name: Chapel
entries.felt: A small European stone chapel - tiled roofs, a little steeple/tower, arched door, ivy at the base. Felt: quiet faith, a village's spiritual center, refuge; humble and warm. The intact counterpart to the church ruins.
entries.use_when: Medieval villages and towns, a roadside chapel, a monastery. Place with graves/cemetery for a churchyard; use the church ruins for its destroyed version. A strong 'settled Christian community' marker.

entries.name: Quarry
entries.felt: Piles of cut stone blocks with picks and a cart. 6 variants. Felt: hard extractive labor, a working stone quarry; the raw material of walls before it's laid. Industrious and rough.
entries.use_when: A stone quarry, a build site's supply, a mining region. Pair with the stone mine (raw), scaffolding/crane (using it), and lumber for a construction economy.

entries.name: Lumber
entries.felt: Stacks of cut logs and timber, an axe among them. 6 variants. Felt: woodcutting labor, a logging camp's yield; felled forest turned to building stock. Rustic industry.
entries.use_when: Logging camps, a sawyer's yard, a build site. Pair with tree stumps/felled trees (source), scaffolding/crane (use), and the quarry for a construction economy.

entries.name: Granary
entries.felt: Round thatched-roof grain-store huts on raised bases, baskets and pots (and a chicken) at the foot. 5 variants. Felt: a village's stored harvest, subsistence secured, African/tribal domestic life. Homely and vital.
entries.use_when: African/tribal villages, a farmstead, a settlement's food store. Cluster with huts, forage, and livestock for a lived-in village; the built counterpart to haystacks.

entries.name: Grain Storage
entries.felt: Dome/beehive grain silos in mudbrick and woven basketry. 6 variants. Felt: ancient food security, the Near-East/African granary; engineered storage, the surplus that builds cities. Earthy and practical.
entries.use_when: Ancient Near-East/African settlements, a temple or palace store, a farming village. Pair with Mesopotamian architecture and the market stalls; the drier-climate cousin of the thatched granary.

entries.name: Furnace
entries.felt: Metalworking furnaces and kilns - chimney furnaces with bellows, a beehive pottery kiln. 5 variants. Felt: fire-driven craft, the smith and potter at work; heat, skill, transformation. The industrial heart of a settlement.
entries.use_when: A smithy, foundry, or pottery, a craftsmen's quarter, a forge. Pair with amphorae/water pots (pottery output), weapon racks (smithing output), and the market. Signals skilled industry.

entries.name: Leatherworking Equipment
entries.felt: A 24-piece tannery/leatherworking kit - hides stretched on frames, drying skins, tanning tables with tools. Felt: a messy skilled craft, the smell-you-can-see of a tannery; animal to leather, patient work. Comprehensive craft-clutter set.
entries.use_when: A tannery, a craftsmen's row, a nomad/steppe camp working hides, a frontier settlement. Assemble the pieces into a working leatherworks; pairs with livestock and the market.

entries.name: Amphorae
entries.felt: Clusters of terracotta amphorae and jars, single and grouped, some on stands. 16 variants. Felt: stored wine and oil, Mediterranean trade and plenty, the classical world's tupperware. Warm terracotta abundance.
entries.use_when: Mediterranean/ancient markets, docks, cellars, a merchant's yard, a villa store. Scatter richly among stalls and barrels; the ceramic-goods counterpart to barrels. Pairs with the furnace (their maker).

entries.name: Water Pots
entries.felt: Grouped clay water pots and jars, some on a stand/frame. 6 variants. Felt: daily household life, fetching and storing water, domestic humility; the vessels beside a well or doorway. Quietly human.
entries.use_when: Village homes, beside a well or fountain, a courtyard, a market. Scatter at doorways and water sources; pairs with the well and benches for domestic detail.

entries.name: Rugs
entries.felt: Flat decorative rugs/carpets - red and gold patterns, a blue one, a rolled one. 6 variants. Felt: warmth underfoot, market wares, domestic comfort and color; a spot of pattern on bare ground. Ground-decal, walkable.
entries.use_when: Markets (goods for sale), a tent or home interior, a merchant's display, an ornate courtyard. Lay flat to warm a space or dress a market stall; one of few textile accents.

entries.name: Construction Crane
entries.felt: Wooden lifting cranes - A-frame and lever hoists with buckets and counterweights raising loads. 8 variants. Felt: a building rising, engineering and labor, momentum; work actively underway. Pairs with scaffolding as the other 'being built' signal.
entries.use_when: An active construction site, a wonder or cathedral going up, a quarry/dock loading goods. Place with scaffolding, stone/lumber piles, and a half-built structure for a living work-site.

entries.name: Sign
entries.felt: Wooden directional signposts, arms pointing various ways. 16 variants (facings/arrangements). Felt: travel, a crossroads decision, human wayfinding; the road goes somewhere. A small storytelling prop - it implies places beyond the frame.
entries.use_when: Crossroads, road forks, a village edge, a traveler's path. Place where roads meet; a signpost quietly says 'there are other places' and orients a scene.

entries.name: Hero Shrine
entries.felt: Small tiled-roof stone shrines on columns over a raised base, some with an offering/relic within, some vine-grown. 12 variants (fresh to weathered). Felt: veneration of a hero or saint, a wayside altar, a place people stop to honor; intimate reverence at a built scale.
entries.use_when: A hero's memorial, a wayside or crossroads shrine, a temple precinct's minor altars, a venerated grave. Place where devotion focuses; the weathered variants read as old/forgotten. Pairs with graves and statues.

entries.name: Gallows
entries.felt: Gallows - a simple gibbet post with a noose, and a full scaffold platform with steps. 4 variants. Felt: harsh justice, public execution, the state's power over life; grim and sobering. Bridges the inhabited world and the death register - a built instrument of death.
entries.use_when: A town square's dark corner, a tyrant's warning, a prison/justice site, a lawless frontier. Use sparingly - one gallows sets a heavy tone; pair with impaled corpses/graves for a place of dread.

entries.name: Gunpowder Keg
entries.felt: Small red gunpowder kegs/barrels, numbered. 6 variants. Felt: volatile danger, a demolition or a siege's explosive stock, imminent violence; a barrel you don't want a spark near. Tense.
entries.use_when: A siege camp, an armory, a mine, a demolition, a powder store. Scatter near siege engines and cannons; signals military tech and hazard. Pairs with the siege sets.

entries.name: Siege Camp Equipment
entries.felt: Siege engines mid-assembly - catapult/trebuchet frames, timber, workbenches. 16 variants. Felt: a siege being prepared, war-machines taking shape, patient destructive intent; the workshop behind an assault.
entries.use_when: A siege camp behind the lines, an army preparing to assault a fortress, a military engineer's yard. Cluster with the other siege sets, weapon racks, and army tents for a besieging force.

entries.name: Siege Camp Clutter
entries.felt: Siege-camp ground clutter - logs, timber piles, a workbench, build materials. 8 variants. Felt: the messy supply-yard of a siege, work in progress, an army's industry; fills the ground of a military camp with purpose.
entries.use_when: Scatter across a siege camp's ground to fill space around the engines and tents; the low-detail connective clutter that makes a camp read as busy and real.

entries.name: Siege Props
entries.felt: Assembled and partial siege engines - catapults, trebuchets, rams in various states. 15 variants. Felt: the machines of siege ready or nearly so, mechanical menace, the tools that break walls. The finished counterpart to the under-construction siege equipment.
entries.use_when: An active siege line, an army camp, a fortress under assault, an arsenal. Place the assembled engines facing a target wall; combine with siege-camp equipment (building) and clutter (ground) for a full siege scene.

entries.name: Pine
entries.felt: A tall conical evergreen pine, 27 variants carrying a state cycle (green -> autumn-gold -> bare brown skeleton). Felt: the workhorse conifer, a northern/temperate pinewood; upright and orderly. The evergreen backbone of a cold or mountain forest.
entries.use_when: Pine forests, boreal/temperate woods, mountain slopes. Mass for a coniferous forest; use the bare/gold frames for autumn or die-off. Pairs with snow pine and mountains.

entries.name: Snow Pine
entries.felt: A snow-dusted pine - white-frosted conifer with bare-winter variants. 27 frames. Felt: deep winter, an alpine or boreal forest under snow; cold, still, beautiful. The winter face of the pinewood.
entries.use_when: Snowy/alpine forests, a winter map, high mountain slopes. Mass with snow-autumn oak and ice decals under the snow-capped mountains for a coherent cold biome.

entries.name: Cypress (natural)
entries.felt: The natural Italian cypress - a tall narrow dark-green columnar spire, 12 height variants. Felt: Mediterranean verticality, cemetery and villa; the same solemn spire as the decorative cypress (2529) in the natural/forest unit. A strong vertical accent.
entries.use_when: Mediterranean/Tuscan landscapes, villa avenues, cemeteries. Line for rhythm against horizontal masses; interchangeable with the decorative cypress. Pairs with olive and Italian pine.

entries.name: Monkey Puzzle
entries.felt: An Araucaria/monkey-puzzle - a tall bare trunk topped by a rounded umbrella of stiff spiky branches. 8 variants. Felt: prehistoric, otherworldly, ancient-lineage; a tree that looks like the age of dinosaurs. Highly distinctive, a conversation-piece landmark.
entries.use_when: Exotic/southern-hemisphere settings, a primeval forest, a strange or fantasy landscape, an arboretum specimen. Place singly as an oddity or cluster for a Jurassic feel.

entries.name: Palm
entries.felt: Coconut/date palms in 39 variants - tall singles, clustered, short, leaning. Felt: tropics, beaches, oases; sun and warmth. A comprehensive palm set for any warm coast or desert spring. Height variety makes natural groves.
entries.use_when: Tropical coasts, islands, oases, desert springs. Cluster with varied heights/leans for a natural beach or oasis; pairs with the wax palm, jungle, and beach karsts.

entries.name: Jungle Tree
entries.felt: Dense jungle trees - broad-leaf canopy mixed with palms and understory, 39 variants. Felt: humid impenetrable jungle, layered green life; the wall of the tropics. Rich enough to build a whole jungle from one unit.
entries.use_when: Jungles and rainforests, tropical river valleys. Mass densely with the jungle floor plants, rainforest trees, and rock-jungle features for an overgrown tropical world.

entries.name: Rainforest Tree
entries.felt: The largest tree set in gaia - 69 variants of rainforest: towering emergent trees, hanging vines, palms, leafy canopy, understory. Felt: a complete rainforest ecosystem in one unit; depth, height, teeming life. The definitive tropical-forest source.
entries.use_when: Deep rainforest, an Amazon/Congo/SE-Asian jungle. The 69 variants mean a huge non-repeating forest from a single unit_const; layer emergents over jungle trees over floor plants for true canopy depth.

entries.name: Mangrove
entries.felt: Mangroves - green canopies on tangled exposed stilt/prop-root systems. 36 variants. Felt: coastal wetland, brackish swamp, the meeting of land and sea; the exposed roots are the whole character - a tree standing on stilts in water. Unmistakable.
entries.use_when: Coastal swamps, river deltas, brackish wetlands, a tropical shore. Place at the waterline where the roots read; cluster for a mangrove forest. Pairs with reeds, water, and shore rocks.

entries.name: Brazilwood
entries.felt: Leafy broadleaf tropical hardwoods with reddish trunks (pau-brasil, the red dyewood). 14 variants. Felt: a valuable tropical hardwood, warm-toned wood under green; New-World tropics and the dye trade. Rounder and more temperate-looking than jungle palms.
entries.use_when: South-American/tropical forests, a valuable-wood grove, a coastal Atlantic forest. Mix with jungle and rainforest for variety, or as a distinct hardwood stand.

entries.name: Lush Bamboo
entries.felt: Dense green living bamboo - tall leafy clumps of stalks, 16 size variants. Felt: an East-Asian bamboo grove, serene and rustling, fast-growing life; a green screen you can almost hear. The living counterpart to the felled/stump bamboo.
entries.use_when: Bamboo groves, East-Asian forests and gardens, a panda habitat, a screen along a path. Mass for a grove; pairs with Asian pine, pagodas, karst pillars, and the bamboo stumps.

entries.name: Felled Bamboo
entries.felt: Cut/fallen bamboo - sparse thin stalks lying and scattered, 9 variants. Felt: harvested bamboo, a worked grove, thinned-out aftermath; the cut counterpart to lush bamboo. Sparse and low.
entries.use_when: A harvested bamboo grove, a woodcutter's/craft site, aftermath of clearing. Scatter among lush bamboo and bamboo stumps for a managed/worked grove.

entries.name: Acacia
entries.felt: Acacias - flat-topped umbrella crowns on bare spreading trunks, 30 variants. Felt: the African savanna itself, the lone tree on the golden plain, sunset silhouette; open dry country and wide horizons. Iconic.
entries.use_when: African savanna, dry grassland, an open plain. Scatter sparsely across dry grass (never dense - savanna trees stand apart); the definitive 'Africa' tree. Pairs with baobab and dry grass.

entries.name: Baobab
entries.felt: Baobabs - the massive swollen bottle-shaped trunk under a sparse crown (the 'upside-down tree'), 45 variants including bare. Felt: ancient African icon, water hoarded in the trunk, a tree older than kingdoms; strange, monumental, unmistakable. A landmark on its own.
entries.use_when: African savanna and dry country, a sacred/landmark tree, a village meeting-tree. Place singly as a focal oddity or dot across a plain; the bare variants read as dry-season. Pairs with acacia and dry grass.

entries.name: Dragon Tree
entries.felt: Dragon trees (Dracaena) - thick trunks branching into umbrellas of stiff spiky rosette crowns, 36 variants with bare/dead at the end. Felt: alien and ancient, a Socotra dreamscape, blood-of-the-dragon myth; exotic and sculptural. Unlike any temperate tree.
entries.use_when: Exotic/fantasy islands, a strange arid landscape, a mythic setting. Place singly or in strange groves for an otherworldly feel; pairs with mesa rocks and dry country. A cousin in strangeness to the monkey puzzle.

entries.name: Autumn Oak
entries.felt: An oak tuned to autumn - 42 variants running the full fall palette (green -> gold -> orange -> red -> bare). Felt: peak autumn woodland, the turning of the year, warm decay; richer fall color than the base Oak. Season made selectable frame by frame.
entries.use_when: Autumn forests, a fall scene, the turning season. Mix frames for a natural color spread (some green, some red, some bare); lay maple-leaf litter beneath. Pairs with the base oak and fallen-leaves decals.

entries.name: Snow Autumn Oak
entries.felt: An oak caught between autumn and winter - turning red/gold foliage DUSTED WITH SNOW, through bare snowy skeletons. 42 variants. Felt: first snow on unfallen leaves, the hinge of the year, cold beauty; the rare and specific mood of late-autumn frost. A distinctive transitional tree.
entries.use_when: The autumn-to-winter transition, a first-snow scene, a cold-temperate forest. Use between the autumn oak (fall) and snow pine (winter) for a seasonal gradient across a map.

entries.name: Asian Maple (Green)
entries.felt: A green Japanese/Asian maple in summer leaf - delicate layered foliage, 9 variants. Felt: an ornamental garden tree, refined and gentle, dappled shade; East-Asian cultivated beauty in its green season. The summer face of the Asian maple.
entries.use_when: East-Asian gardens, a temple courtyard, an ornamental accent by water or stone. Place as a chosen specimen; pairs with the pavilion, stone lanterns, and (its autumn twin) the Asian maple autumn.

entries.name: Asian Maple (Autumn)
entries.felt: The Asian maple in autumn - blazing crimson, orange, gold and transitional greens, 18 variants. Felt: the iconic Japanese momiji, fire-colored and exquisite, the most vivid fall foliage in gaia; refined melancholy beauty. A showpiece.
entries.use_when: East-Asian autumn scenes, a temple garden in fall, a showpiece focal tree. A single crimson maple is a strong focal point; mix the 18 for a natural color range. Pairs with peach-blossom (its spring counterpart) and the garden pieces.

entries.name: Peach Blossom
entries.felt: A peach/cherry tree in full pink bloom - a cloud of blossom over a dark trunk, 5 variants. Felt: spring, sakura, fleeting beauty and renewal; romance and transience. The spring showpiece, counterpart to the autumn maple.
entries.use_when: Spring scenes, East-Asian gardens and orchards, a romantic or festival setting (recall Buddha B's sakura courtyard). Cluster for a blossoming orchard; lay the peach-blossom petal decal beneath. Pairs with the meru pagoda and garden pieces.

entries.name: Reeds
entries.felt: Golden marsh reeds - wispy tall reed/cattail clumps, 12 variants. Felt: a water's edge, marsh and riverbank, wind over wetland; soft, dry-gold, transitional between land and water. Despite the 'tree' filename it is water-edge grass.
entries.use_when: Riverbanks, marshes, pond and lake edges, a swamp. Line the waterline in clumps; pairs with mangroves, water lily, fish traps, and shore rocks for a wetland shore.

entries.name: Dead Tree
entries.felt: A dedicated dead-tree set - bare leafless skeletons from full standing dead trees to weathered snags, grey and brown, 21 variants. Felt: desolation, blight, drought, the aftermath of fire or time; more varied and detailed than the scenario dead trees. Mood over species.
entries.use_when: Wastelands, blighted or burned forest, swamp, winter kill, a haunted wood. Scatter singly for a hint of death among the living, or mass for a dead forest. Pairs with dead plants, the death batch, and burned buildings.

entries.name: Macedonian Flag
entries.felt: A waving banner bearing the Vergina Sun - the radiant 16-ray star of Macedon - animated across 270 frames. Felt: Hellenistic identity, Alexander's standard, a named people's claim on ground; more specific than the generic flags - this banner says WHO holds this place. One of the city/faction flag family (Athenian, Spartan, Achaemenid, etc.).
entries.use_when: A Macedonian/Hellenistic camp, city, or army; a faction marker where the culture matters. Plant at a command tent, gate, or held position. Use the other city flags for other factions to color a mixed battlefield.

entries.name: Ballista
entries.felt: A ballista/bolt-thrower artillery engine (animated unit, 961 idle frames across facings). Felt: ancient siege artillery ready to loose, mechanical menace on the line; the assembled, manned counterpart to the under-construction siege props. Poised violence.
entries.use_when: A siege line or army camp facing a wall, a fortress defense, an arsenal. Place assembled ballistae aimed at a target with the siege-prop engines and camp equipment for a full siege scene; pairs with weapon racks and gunpowder kegs.

entries.name: Cactus
entries.felt: Cacti in 11 variants - tall columnar saguaros, low prickly-pear clumps, barrel cacti, some flowering red. Felt: the desert made green, thorny survival, dry heat; the signature plant of arid country. Varied enough to build a whole desert flora.
entries.use_when: Deserts, badlands, arid mesas, an oasis edge. Scatter with dry grass, mesa rocks, and sand cliffs; the saguaros as vertical accents, prickly-pears as ground scatter.

entries.name: Forage Fruit Bush
entries.felt: A low dense bush heavy with yellow fruit, 4 variants. Felt: forageable plenty, an orchard hedge, autumn harvest; food hanging ready to pick. Warmer and more bountiful than the plain berry bush.
entries.use_when: Foraging spots near a settlement, an orchard edge, a fruitful hedge. Cluster for a productive patch; the fruit-laden cousin of the forage berry bush.

entries.name: Forage Papaya
entries.felt: A papaya plant - a leafy palm-like top with clusters of hanging orange fruit on a slender stalk, 4 variants. Felt: tropical abundance, exotic food, a jungle larder; distinct and recognizable. The tropical forage counterpart to the fruit bush.
entries.use_when: Tropical/jungle settlements as forageable food, a plantation, a village garden in the tropics. Scatter near huts and jungle edges; pairs with pineapple and jungle greenery.

entries.name: Oysters
entries.felt: Clusters of oyster/shellfish - golden-brown shell clumps with hints of pink flesh, 4 variants. Felt: a tidal shellfish bed, coastal foraging, the shore's quiet larder; low and clustered at the waterline. Marine food that isn't a fish.
entries.use_when: Tidal flats, a rocky shore, a coastal village's shellfish beds, an estuary. Place at the waterline with sea rocks and reeds; a shore-food resource distinct from the fish.

entries.name: Fern Patch (Rainforest)
entries.felt: A broad spread of rainforest ferns and leafy plants, 3 variants. Felt: the humid forest floor carpeted in green, dappled understory; lush ground cover for the tropics. Wider-area than a single fern.
entries.use_when: Rainforest and jungle floors as a base ground layer under trees; lay for lush understory, then stand jungle/rainforest trees on top. Pairs with the underbrush mats.

entries.name: Flowerbed
entries.felt: A cultivated patch of mixed flowers and greenery, red and yellow blooms scattered through, 3 variants. Felt: a tended garden bed, deliberate cheer, human care; arranged rather than wild. A spread of color for a cultivated space.
entries.use_when: Gardens, a palace or villa's beds, a tended courtyard, around a fountain or shrine. Lay as cultivated color; the arranged counterpart to wild meadow flowers.

entries.name: Flower Patch 1
entries.felt: A large dense carpet of wildflowers - green ground thick with small red blooms. Felt: a wild meadow in flower, spring abundance, open color; a big-area spread, not a single tuft. One of four wildflower carpets.
entries.use_when: Meadows, open fields, a spring hillside. Lay large areas for a flowering meadow; use with the other flower patches (2-4) for natural variation. The big-carpet cousin of the small flower tuft.

entries.name: Flower Patch 2
entries.felt: A second large wildflower carpet - green with red blooms, a slightly different spread and density than patch 1. Felt: wild meadow color; interchangeable with the other flower patches for variety.
entries.use_when: Meadows and fields; alternate with flower patches 1/3/4 so a large flowering area does not visibly repeat.

entries.name: Flower Patch 3
entries.felt: A third wildflower carpet variant - green ground with scattered red blooms. Felt: wild meadow color; part of the 4-patch set for non-repeating flowering ground.
entries.use_when: Meadows and fields; rotate with patches 1/2/4 for natural variation across a large flowering area.

entries.name: Flower Patch 4
entries.felt: The fourth wildflower carpet - green with red blooms, its own spread pattern. Felt: wild meadow color; completes the 4-patch set for varied flowering ground.
entries.use_when: Meadows and fields; use all four flower patches together for the most natural large flowering meadow.

entries.name: Grass Patch (Green)
entries.felt: A large spread of green grass - a meadow carpet, not a single tuft. Felt: a healthy field, lush pasture, living ground over a wide area. The big-area version of the small green grass tuft.
entries.use_when: Cover large fields and clearings efficiently with one placement; the area-fill counterpart to the small grass tufts. Blend with the dry patch at edges for a moisture gradient.

entries.name: Grass Patch (Dry)
entries.felt: A large spread of dry golden grass - a sun-bleached meadow carpet. Felt: steppe, savanna, late summer, arid plain over a wide area. The big-area dry-grass carpet.
entries.use_when: Steppe, savanna, dry plains, arid fields - cover large areas in one placement. Blend with the green grass patch for a green-to-dry gradient; pairs with acacia and dry country.

entries.name: Ice
entries.felt: Flat ice floes/patches - white-blue frozen sheets and chunks, 7 variants. Felt: frozen water, arctic cold, a winter thaw or freeze; a flat decal for water or ground. The frozen counterpart to open water.
entries.use_when: Frozen lakes/seas, an arctic map, a winter river, a glacier's edge. Lay on water for ice floes or on ground for frozen patches; pairs with snow trees, snow-capped mountains, and snow cliffs.

entries.name: Fish (Dorado)
entries.felt: Small green-blue dorado/mahi-mahi (animated swim). Felt: a shoal of food beneath the surface, a fisher's catch, life in the water. A gatherable marine food resource; tiny individually, meaningful in numbers.
entries.use_when: Warm seas and coasts as a fishing resource; scatter a shoal near a fishing village or dock. One of several fish species keyed to different waters.

entries.name: Fish (Marlin)
entries.felt: A blue marlin - a larger billfish with a spear-bill (animated). Felt: a prize game-fish, deep open water, a bigger catch than the shoal fish; the trophy of the sea. More substantial than the small food fish.
entries.use_when: Deep/open ocean, a rich fishing ground, a big-game fishing spot. Place in deeper water away from shore as a larger resource; pairs with the whale and the smaller fish.

entries.name: Fish (Perch)
entries.felt: A small greenish perch (animated). Felt: freshwater life, a river or pond fish, humble catch; the everyday inland food fish. Small and unglamorous.
entries.use_when: Rivers, ponds, lakes as a freshwater fishing resource. Scatter in inland water near a village; the freshwater counterpart to the marine fish.

entries.name: Fish (Salmon)
entries.felt: A silvery salmon (animated). Felt: a river run, migratory plenty, a northern staple; the fish of cold rivers and returns. Clean silver.
entries.use_when: Cold rivers and streams, a salmon run, a northern fishing spot. Scatter in flowing freshwater; pairs with pine/snow settings and a fishing village.

entries.name: Fish (Snapper)
entries.felt: A red snapper - reddish-pink reef fish (animated; clear on the sampled sheet). Felt: a prized coastal reef catch, warm color in the shallows; more of a delicacy than the workaday tuna/perch. Near-shore marine food.
entries.use_when: Coastal shallows and reefs as a fishing resource; scatter near shore with the other marine fish for a varied catch.

entries.name: Fish (Tuna)
entries.felt: A dark tuna (animated). Felt: open-sea food fish, a shoaling staple, the bulk catch of a sea people; workaday marine abundance.
entries.use_when: Open sea and coasts as a staple fishing resource; scatter shoals off a fishing village. Part of the marine fish set (dorado/snapper/tuna) for near-to-open water.

entries.name: Whale
entries.felt: A grey whale (animated swim) - the giant of the sea. Felt: a leviathan of the deep, a huge windfall of food, awe at scale; the living counterpart to the beached-whale carcass. The richest single marine resource.
entries.use_when: Deep ocean as a large fishing/whaling resource, a sense of a living deep sea. Place in deep water away from shore; pairs with the marlin and (as its death) the beached whale.

entries.name: Howler Monkey
entries.felt: An ANIMATED jungle habitat vignette (clear on the sampled sheet): monkeys living in their own tree-and-fallen-log scene, climbing and moving through it. Like the panda habitat, it is a self-contained living diorama you place WHOLE, not ambient scatter-critters. Felt: the jungle canopy alive with motion, a window into wild life; charming and complete.
entries.use_when: A focal jungle-wildlife moment - drop the whole habitat vignette (its own monkeys + trees + log) as a living landmark in a rainforest. Place singly; do not scatter as individual critters.

entries.name: Panda Rock
entries.felt: An ANIMATED habitat vignette (human-identified): a lovely little scene - a bamboo-and-rock habitat with pandas WANDERING AROUND in it. Not a static critter or rock but a self-contained living diorama that plays out on its own. Felt: gentle life, a window into a wild corner, a scene rather than an object; charming and whole. You place the whole habitat, not a single animal.
entries.use_when: A focal wildlife moment in an East-Asian/bamboo-forest scene - drop the whole habitat as a self-contained living vignette (its own pandas + rocks + setting). Place singly as a charming landmark; do not treat it as a scatter-critter. Pairs with lush bamboo and mountains.
entries.source: In-game visual identification; AoE2Kit sprite render.

entries.name: Flag B
entries.felt: A pale pennant-style banner waving on a pole (animated). Felt: a claim or muster point, motion in the wind; a lighter, more triangular cloth than Flag A. Blank canvas for a held position. Part of the generic flag family (a-u).
entries.use_when: Mark camps, rally points, held ground, a gate. A pennant shape where Flag A's square banner is too heavy; use city flags (Macedonian etc.) when the faction matters.

entries.name: Flag C
entries.felt: A grey rectangular banner on a pole (animated). Felt: a plain standard, a neutral marker, wind and claim; the boxier cloth of the flag family. Another blank-banner option for held ground.
entries.use_when: Mark positions, camps, borders; pick the flag shape (A square / B pennant / C rectangular) that suits the scene. Faction flags for named cultures.

size_landscape.note: gaia subset ~1.2GB; per-pick pull (~1s each) for the walk, full local cache optional
